title.zh: 卷一百九十五 志第一百四十八 兵九
title.raw: 卷一百九十五 志第一百四十八 兵九 Volume 195 Treatises 148: Military 9

sentences.zh: 訓練之制

translations.literal: Regulations on training.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations on Military Training

sentences.zh: 禁軍月奉五百以上，皆日習武技。

translations.literal: For the Imperial Guard, those with monthly pay of five hundred [cash] and above all practiced martial skills daily.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the Imperial Guard who received five hundred cash or more per month were required to drill in martial skills every day.

sentences.zh: 三百以下，或給役，或習技。

translations.literal: Those below three hundred [cash] either performed labor service or practiced skills.
translations.idiomatic: Those paid less than three hundred cash either performed corvée duties or trained in military skills.

sentences.zh: 其後別募廂兵，亦閱習武技，號教閱廂軍。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when separately recruiting garrison troops, they also reviewed and practiced martial skills, called instruction-review garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when garrison troops were recruited separately, they too were drilled in martial skills; these units were designated instruction-review garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 戍川、廣者舊不訓練，嘉祐以後稍習焉。

translations.literal: Those garrisoned in Sichuan and Guang [regions] were formerly not trained; after the Jiayou era they gradually practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Troops stationed in Sichuan and Guangdong had traditionally received no drill, but after the Jiayou period they gradually began training.

sentences.zh: 凡諸日習之法，以鼓聲為節，騎兵五習，步兵四習，以其坐作進退非施於兩軍相當者然。

translations.literal: As for all methods of daily practice, drumbeats set the pace; cavalry had five exercises and infantry four exercises, because their sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating were not applied when two armies faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Daily drill followed drum cadence: cavalry practiced five routines and infantry four, since these formations for sitting, standing, advancing, and retreating were not the same as maneuvers used when two armies met in battle.

sentences.zh: 自宋初以來，中外諸軍皆用之。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the Song, all armies inside and outside [the capital] used them.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of the dynasty onward, all armies throughout the empire adopted these methods.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，樞密使王曙言：“天下廂軍止給役而未嚐習武技，宜取材勇者訓肄，升補禁軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao, Privy Councillor Wang Shu said: Garrison troops throughout the realm only perform labor service and have never practiced martial skills; one should select brave men for training and promotion to supplement the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1033, Privy Councillor Wang Shu memorialized: Garrison troops across the empire perform only corvée labor and have never been drilled in martial skills. Brave men should be selected for training and promoted into the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: ”上可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，帝御便殿閱諸軍陣法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, the emperor received [troops] at the informal hall to review all armies' battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1040, the emperor reviewed army battle formations in the informal audience hall.

sentences.zh: 議者謂諸軍止教坐作進退，雖整肅可觀，然臨敵難用，請自今遣官閱陣畢，令解鐙以弓弩射。

translations.literal: Discussants said the armies only taught sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating; though orderly and impressive to view, they were hard to use facing the enemy. They requested that from now on, after officials finished reviewing formations, [troops] be ordered to dismount from stirrups and shoot with bow and crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that troops were drilled only in ceremonial marching, which looked impressive but would prove useless in combat. They proposed that after formation reviews, soldiers should dismount and practice shooting with bows and crossbows.

sentences.zh: 營置弓三等，自一石至八斗；

translations.literal: Camps were to provide bows in three grades, from one picul to eight tenths [of a picul];
translations.idiomatic: Each camp was to stock three grades of bow, ranging from one picul draw weight down to eight-tenths of a picul;

sentences.zh: 弩四等，自二石八斗至二石五斗，以次閱習。

translations.literal: crossbows in four grades, from two piculs eight tenths to two piculs five tenths, to be reviewed and practiced in order.
translations.idiomatic: and four grades of crossbow, from two piculs eight tenths down to two piculs five tenths, with men trained on each grade in succession.

sentences.zh: 詔行之陝西、河東、河北路。

translations.literal: An edict ordered implementation in the Shaanxi, Hedong, and Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered these measures implemented in the Shaanxi, Hedong, and Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔：“教士不衽帶金革，緩急不足以應敵。

translations.literal: That year, an edict said: Training soldiers without wearing armor and weapons is insufficient to meet the enemy in emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: That same year an edict declared: Soldiers who drill without wearing armor and weapons will be unprepared when battle comes.

sentences.zh: 自今諸軍各予鎧甲十、馬甲五，令迭披帶。

translations.literal: From now on each army is to be given ten suits of armor and five horse armors, and ordered to wear them in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth each army unit is to receive ten suits of body armor and five horse armors, with troops taking turns wearing them during drill.

sentences.zh: ”又命諸軍班聽習雜武技，勿輒禁止。

translations.literal: It also ordered all army companies to be permitted to practice miscellaneous martial skills, and not to be forbidden arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were also permitted to practice assorted martial skills in their companies without arbitrary prohibition.

sentences.zh: 慶曆元年，徙邊兵不教者於內郡，俟習武技即遣戍邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingli, border soldiers who were not trained were transferred to inner prefectures; once they had practiced martial skills they were sent to garrison the border.
translations.idiomatic: In 1041, border troops who had received no training were transferred to interior prefectures and, once they had mastered martial skills, were sent back to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 二年，諸軍以射親疏為賞罰，中的者免是月諸役，仍籍其名。

translations.literal: In the second year, all armies used closeness of shooting as reward and punishment; those who hit the mark were exempted from all duties that month, and their names were registered.
translations.idiomatic: In 1042, armies began rewarding and punishing troops based on close-range shooting accuracy. Those who hit the target were exempted from all corvée duties for that month, and their names were recorded.

sentences.zh: 闕校長，則按籍取中多者補。

translations.literal: When company commanders were vacant, names were taken from the register of those with the most hits to fill [the posts].
translations.idiomatic: When a company commander's post fell vacant, the man with the most recorded hits was promoted to fill it.

sentences.zh: 樞密直學士楊偕請教騎兵止射九斗至七鬥三等弓，畫的為五暈，去的二十步，引滿即發，射中者，視暈數給錢為賞。

translations.literal: Privy Council academician Yang Jie requested that cavalry be taught to shoot only three grades of bow from nine tenths to seven tenths [of a picul]; the target was drawn with five rings; at twenty paces distance, upon drawing full they were to release; those who hit were rewarded with money according to the number of rings.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council academician Yang Jie proposed that cavalry be trained on three grades of bow ranging from nine-tenths to seven-tenths of a picul. The target was marked with five concentric rings at twenty paces; archers drew to full draw and released immediately. Hits were rewarded in cash according to which ring was struck.

sentences.zh: 騎兵佩劈陣刀，訓肄時以木杆代之。

translations.literal: Cavalry wore array-breaking sabers; during training wooden staffs were substituted.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry carried array-breaking sabers; during drill wooden staffs were used in their place.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：“騎兵帶甲射不能發矢者，奪所乘馬與本營藝優士卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict said: Cavalry who shoot in armor but cannot release an arrow shall have their mount taken and given to skilled soldiers of their own camp.
translations.idiomatic: In 1044, an edict declared: Any cavalryman who cannot loose an arrow while wearing armor shall forfeit his mount to the most skilled archer in his camp.

sentences.zh: ”韓琦言：“教射唯事體容及強弓，不習射親不可以臨陣。

translations.literal: Han Qi said: Teaching archery attends only to posture and powerful bows; without practicing close-range shooting one cannot face battle.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi argued: Archery drill today emphasizes posture and heavy bows alone. Troops who never practice close-range shooting cannot be sent into battle.

sentences.zh: 臣至邊，嚐定弓弩挽強、蹠硬、射親格，願行諸軍立賞肄習。

translations.literal: When your servant reached the border, I once set standards for bow and crossbow draw-strength, foot-stomp hardness, and close-range shooting; I wish to implement them in all armies with rewards established for practice.
translations.idiomatic: When I reached the frontier, I established standards for bow draw weight, crossbow foot-stomp force, and close-range shooting accuracy. I ask that these standards be applied across all armies with rewards offered for diligent practice.

sentences.zh: 歲以春秋二時各一閱，諸營先上射親吏卒之數，命近臣與殿前、馬步軍司閱之。

translations.literal: Each year in spring and autumn there would be one review each; all camps first submitted the number of officers and soldiers proficient in close-range shooting; nearby ministers and the Bureau of the Palace, Cavalry, and Infantry were ordered to review them.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn a review would be held. Every camp would first report how many officers and men had qualified in close-range shooting, and court officials together with the Palace, Cavalry, and Infantry Bureaus would conduct the inspection.

sentences.zh: 其射親入第四至第七等，量先給賜；

translations.literal: Those whose close-range shooting reached the fourth through seventh grades would receive rewards in proportion beforehand;
translations.idiomatic: Men who qualified in close-range shooting at grades four through seven would receive preliminary rewards in proportion to their grade;

sentences.zh: 入第三等已上及挽強、蹠硬中格，悉引對親閱；

translations.literal: those who reached the third grade and above, and those who met the standard in draw-strength and foot-stomp hardness, would all be presented for personal review;
translations.idiomatic: those who reached grade three or above, or who met the standards for bow draw weight and crossbow foot-stomp force, would all be presented to the emperor for personal inspection;

sentences.zh: 等數多者，其正副指揮使亦第賜金帛。

translations.literal: for those with many [high] grades, their chief and deputy commanders would also receive ranked gifts of gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: and commanders whose units produced the greatest number of high-grade performers would themselves receive graded gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: ”詔以所定格班教諸軍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the established grade standards taught to all armies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all armies trained according to these established grade standards.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣官以陝西陣法分教河北軍士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, officials were dispatched to teach Hebei soldiers separately using Shaanxi battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1044, officials were dispatched to teach Hebei troops the battle formations used in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 五年，密詔益、利、梓、夔路鈐轄司，以弓弩習士卒，候民間觀聽浸熟，即便以短兵日教三十人，十日一易。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, a secret edict to the supervisory offices of the Yi, Li, Zi, and Kui circuits ordered training soldiers with bow and crossbow; when popular observation had gradually become familiar, then daily teach thirty men in short weapons, changing every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In 1045, a secret edict to the supervisory commissioners of the Yi, Li, Zi, and Kui circuits ordered troops trained with bows and crossbows. Once the local population had grown accustomed to seeing the drills, thirty men per day were to be trained in close combat weapons, with the group rotated every ten days.

sentences.zh: 知并州明鎬言：“臣近籍諸營武藝之卒，使帶甲試充奇兵外，為三等，庶幾主將悉知軍中武技強弱，臨敵可用。

translations.literal: Bingzhou prefect Ming Hao said: Your servant recently registered skilled soldiers of all camps, had them try on armor and be tested as elite troops, and divided them into three grades, so that commanders might fully know the strengths and weaknesses of martial skills in the army and use them facing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou prefect Ming Hao reported: I have recently registered the most skilled soldiers in every camp, tested them in armor for assignment as elite troops, and divided them into three grades so that commanders may know precisely which men are strongest and weakest in martial skill and deploy them effectively in battle.

sentences.zh: ”詔頒其法三路。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his method promulgated in the three circuits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his method promulgated across all three frontier circuits.

sentences.zh: 範仲淹請以帶甲射一石充奇兵，餘自九斗至七鬥第為三等，射力及等即升之。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan requested that those who shot one picul in armor serve as elite troops; the rest from nine tenths to seven tenths were ranked in three grades, and upon reaching the grade in shooting strength they were promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan proposed that any soldier who could shoot a one-picul bow in armor be classified as an elite trooper. The remainder, graded from nine-tenths down to seven-tenths of a picul in three tiers, would be promoted as soon as they met the standard for their grade.

sentences.zh: 詔著為令。

translations.literal: An edict established it as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict codified this as permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔諸軍夏三月毋教弓弩，止習短兵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered all armies not to teach bow and crossbow in the third month of summer, practicing only short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In 1046, an edict forbade bow and crossbow drill during the third month of summer; troops were to practice only close-combat weapons.

sentences.zh: 又詔：“以春秋大教弓射一石四斗、弩廣三石八斗、槍刀手勝三人者，立為武藝出眾格。

translations.literal: Another edict said: In the great spring and autumn reviews, those who shot one picul four tenths with bow, drew crossbow three piculs eight tenths wide, or as spearmen and sabermen defeated three men, were established as the outstanding martial-skill grade.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict declared: At the major spring and autumn reviews, any archer who shot a one-picul-four-tenths bow, any crossbowman who drew a three-picul-eight-tenths weapon, or any spearman or saberman who defeated three opponents would qualify for the outstanding martial skill grade.

sentences.zh: 中者，本營闕階級即以次補。

translations.literal: Those who qualified, when ranks were vacant in their camp, were promoted in order to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Qualified men would be promoted in order of merit whenever a rank fell vacant in their camp.

sentences.zh: 至和元年，詔：“諸軍選將校，武藝鈞，以射親為上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe, an edict said: When all armies select officers, if martial skills are equal, close-range shooting takes precedence.
translations.idiomatic: In 1054, an edict declared: When selecting officers from the ranks, if candidates are equal in martial skill, close-range shooting proficiency shall be the deciding factor.

sentences.zh: ”韓琦又言：“奉詔，軍士弩廣四石二斗並弓箭、槍手應舊規選中者，即給挺補守闕押官，然則排連舊制為虛文矣。

translations.literal: Han Qi again said: According to the edict, soldiers whose crossbow draw was four piculs two tenths wide, and archers and spearmen who met the old regulations and were selected, were immediately given tally-sticks and appointed acting deputy officers on the waiting list; thus the old platoon and company system became empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi added: Under the edict, any soldier who draws a four-picul-two-tenths crossbow, or any archer or spearman who meets the old selection standards, is immediately given an officer's tally and appointed acting deputy on the waiting list. This renders the old platoon and company promotion system meaningless.

sentences.zh: 請三路兵遇春秋大教，武技出眾者優給賞物，免本營他役，候階級闕，如舊制選補。

translations.literal: He requested that when the three circuits' troops encountered the great spring and autumn reviews, those outstanding in martial skill receive preferential gifts, be exempted from other duties in their camp, and when ranks were vacant be selected and promoted according to the old system.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that at the major spring and autumn reviews on the three frontier circuits, soldiers of outstanding martial skill receive preferential rewards and exemption from other camp duties, and that when ranks fall vacant they be promoted according to the established system.

sentences.zh: ”奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，詔：“河北戰卒三十萬一千、陝西四十五萬九百並義勇等，委總管司訓練，毋得冗占。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, an edict said: Hebei's combat soldiers numbering 301,000, Shaanxi's 450,900 together with militia and the like, are entrusted to the overall command offices for training, and must not be redundantly occupied.
translations.idiomatic: In 1065, an edict declared: Hebei's 301,000 combat troops, Shaanxi's 450,900, together with militia and similar forces, are entrusted to the overall command offices for training and must not be diverted to non-military duties.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，詔曰：“國家置兵以備戰守，而主兵之官冗占者眾，肄習弗時，或誤軍事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, an edict said: The state maintains armies to prepare for war and defense, yet many officers in charge of troops are redundantly occupied; practice is not timely, and military affairs may be hindered.
translations.idiomatic: In 1068, an edict declared: The state maintains armies for war and defense, yet many officers in command of troops are diverted to non-military duties, drill is neglected, and military readiness suffers.

sentences.zh: 帥臣、安撫、監司其察所部有占兵不如令者以聞。

translations.literal: Commanders, pacification commissioners, and supervisory officials shall investigate their jurisdictions for those who occupy troops contrary to regulations and report.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders, pacification commissioners, and supervisory officials shall investigate their jurisdictions for violations of these regulations and report them.

sentences.zh: ”十月，樞密院請陝西、河東選三班使臣及士人任殿侍者，以為河北諸路指使，教習騎軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the Bureau of Military Affairs requested that Shaanxi and Hedong select third-rank envoys and scholars serving as palace attendants to serve as instructors for the various Hebei circuits, teaching cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the Bureau of Military Affairs proposed that Shaanxi and Hedong select third-rank envoys and scholars serving as palace attendants to serve as drill instructors for the Hebei circuits in cavalry training.

sentences.zh: 或言河朔兵有教閱之名而無其實，請班教法於其軍，久而弗能者，罷為廂軍。

translations.literal: Someone said the Hebei-Shandong troops had the name of instruction-review but not the reality; they requested assigning teaching methods to their armies, and those who after a long time could not [master them] be demoted to garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials reported that Hebei troops bore the title of instruction-review units but received no actual training. They proposed assigning drill instructors to these armies and demoting to garrison status any soldier who failed to master the skills within a reasonable time.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 二年，帝常語執政：“並邊訓練士卒，何以得其精熟？

translations.literal: In the second year, the emperor often said to the chief ministers: Training soldiers on the combined border, how can they be made thoroughly skilled?
translations.idiomatic: In 1069, the emperor often asked his chief ministers: How can we bring frontier troops to full martial proficiency?

sentences.zh: ”安石對曰：“京東所教兵已精強，願陛下推此法以責邊將，間詔其兵親臨閱試。

translations.literal: An Shi replied: The troops taught in Jingdong are already elite and strong; I wish Your Majesty would extend this method to hold border generals responsible, and occasionally summon their troops for personal review and testing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replied: The troops trained in Jingdong are already highly skilled. Your Majesty should extend this system to hold frontier commanders accountable and occasionally summon their troops for personal inspection.

sentences.zh: 訓練簡閱有不如詔者罰之，而賞其能者。

translations.literal: Those whose training and selection-review fell short of the edict were to be punished, while the capable were rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders whose troops fail to meet drill standards should be punished, while those whose units excel should be rewarded.

sentences.zh: 賞不遣賤，罰不避貴，則法行而將吏加勸，士卒無不奮勵矣。

translations.literal: If rewards did not omit the lowly and punishments did not avoid the noble, then the law would be enforced and generals and officers would be further encouraged, and no soldier would fail to strive.
translations.idiomatic: If rewards reach even the humblest soldier and punishments fall even on the highest officers, the regulations will be enforced, commanders will be motivated, and every soldier will strive to excel.

sentences.zh: ”九月，選置指使巡教諸軍，殿前司四人，馬、步軍司各三人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, instructors were selected and appointed to tour and teach all armies: four from the Palace Bureau, three each from the Cavalry and Infantry Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, drill instructors were appointed to tour all armies: four from the Palace Guard Bureau and three each from the Cavalry and Infantry Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 三年，帝親閱河東所教排手，進退輕捷，不畏矢石。

translations.literal: In the third year, the emperor personally reviewed the shield-bearers taught in Hedong; their advance and retreat were light and agile, and they did not fear arrows and stones.
translations.idiomatic: In 1070, the emperor personally reviewed shield-bearers trained in Hedong. Their maneuvers were swift and agile, and they showed no fear of arrows or stones.

sentences.zh: 遂詔殿前司，步軍指揮當出戍者，內擇槍刀手伉健者百人，教如河東法，藝精者免役使，以優獎之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict to the Palace Bureau: among infantry commands about to go on garrison duty, select within them one hundred robust spearmen and sabermen, teach them by the Hedong method; those skilled in the art were exempted from labor service as preferential reward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Palace Guard Bureau to select one hundred robust spearmen and sabermen from infantry units about to deploy on garrison duty, train them by the Hedong method, and exempt the most skilled from corvée labor as a reward.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，詔在京殿前馬步諸軍巡教使臣，並以春秋分行校試。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, an edict ordered touring instructors of all Palace, Cavalry, and Infantry armies in the capital to conduct graded testing separately in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In April 1072, an edict ordered drill instructors for all capital armies of the Palace, Cavalry, and Infantry Bureaus to conduct graded examinations in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 射命中者第賜銀楪，兵房置籍考校，以多少定殿最。

translations.literal: Those who hit the mark in shooting received ranked gifts of silver dishes; the barracks office kept registers for examination, determining best and worst by number.
translations.idiomatic: Archers who hit their targets received graded silver dish rewards. Barracks offices kept score registers, with overall rankings determined by the number of hits.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔以涇原路蔡挺衙教陣隊於崇政殿引見，仍頒諸路。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict ordered the formation teams instructed at Cai Ting's yamen in Jingyuan circuit to be presented at Chongzheng Hall, and still promulgated to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In May, troops trained in battle formations under Cai Ting in Jingyuan circuit were presented at Chongzheng Hall, and the formation method was promulgated to all circuits.

sentences.zh: 其法：五伍為隊，五隊為陣，陣橫列，騎兵二隊亦五伍列之。

translations.literal: The method: five groups of five formed a squad; five squads formed a formation; formations were arrayed horizontally; two cavalry squads were also arrayed in groups of five.
translations.idiomatic: The method organized troops in squads of five, five squads in a formation arrayed horizontally, with two cavalry squads similarly arranged in groups of five.

sentences.zh: 其出皆以鼓為節，束草象人而射焉，中者有賞。

translations.literal: Their deployment all used drums as pace; bundles of straw imitating human figures were shot at, and those who hit received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: All maneuvers followed drum cadence. Bundles of straw shaped like human figures served as targets; hits were rewarded.

sentences.zh: 馬步皆前三行槍刀，後二行弓弩，附隊以虎蹲弩、床子弩各一，射與擊刺迭出，皆聞金即退。

translations.literal: Both cavalry and infantry had the front three ranks with spear and saber, the rear two ranks with bow and crossbow; attached to each squad was one crouching-tiger crossbow and one bed-frame crossbow; shooting and thrusting alternated in deployment, and all withdrew upon hearing the gong.
translations.idiomatic: Both cavalry and infantry placed spearmen and sabermen in the front three ranks and archers in the rear two. Each squad carried one crouching-tiger crossbow and one bed-frame crossbow. Shooting and thrusting alternated in sequence, and all withdrew at the sound of the gong.

sentences.zh: 預籍人馬之強者隱於隊中，遇可用，則別出為奇。

translations.literal: Strong men and horses registered beforehand were concealed within squads; when usable, they were separately deployed as surprise forces.
translations.idiomatic: The strongest men and horses were registered in advance and concealed within squads, to be deployed separately as surprise forces when needed.

sentences.zh: 帝以其點閱周悉，常有出野之備，故令頒行。

translations.literal: The emperor, because their muster-review was thorough and complete and they were always prepared for field deployment, therefore ordered promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged their drill thorough and always ready for field deployment, and ordered the method promulgated empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔：“河北四路承平日久，重於改作，苟遂因循，益隳軍製。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict said: The four Hebei circuits have enjoyed peace for long; they attach weight to avoiding change; if they continue in routine, the military system will further decay.
translations.idiomatic: In 1073, an edict declared: The four Hebei circuits have enjoyed peace so long that they resist innovation. Continued inertia will only further erode military readiness.

sentences.zh: 其以京東武衛等六十二營隸屬諸路，分番教習，餘軍並分遣主兵官訓練。

translations.literal: Let the sixty-two camps such as the Jingdong Martial Guard be subordinated to the various circuits, taught in rotating shifts, and the remaining armies all have officers in charge of troops dispatched separately for training.
translations.idiomatic: The sixty-two camps of the Jingdong Martial Guard and similar units are to be assigned to the various circuits for rotating drill, while all remaining armies are to receive dedicated training officers.

sentences.zh: ”九月，詔：“自今巡教使臣校殿最，雖以十分為率，其事藝第一等及九分已上，或射親及四分，雖殿，除其罰；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict said: From now on when touring instructors grade best and worst on a scale of ten parts, if martial skill reached the first grade and nine parts or above, or close-range shooting reached four parts, even if ranked last, their punishment was remitted;
translations.idiomatic: In September, an edict declared: When touring instructors rank units on a ten-point scale, any unit whose troops achieve first-grade martial skill at nine points or above, or close-range shooting at four points, shall be exempt from punishment even if ranked last overall;

sentences.zh: 第二等事藝及八分，或射親不及三分，雖最，削其賞。

translations.literal: if second-grade martial skill and eight parts, or close-range shooting did not reach three parts, even if ranked first, their reward was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: but any unit ranked first overall whose martial skill reaches only second grade at eight points, or whose close-range shooting falls below three points, shall have its reward reduced.

sentences.zh: ”十月，選涇原士兵之善射者，以教河朔騎軍馳驟野戰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, skilled archers among Jingyuan soldiers were selected to teach Hebei-Shandong cavalry in galloping and field battle.
translations.idiomatic: In October, skilled archers from Jingyuan were selected to train Hebei cavalry in mounted galloping and field combat.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“裁並軍營，凡省軍員四千餘人，此十萬軍之資也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: Cutting and merging army camps, in all over four thousand military personnel were saved; this is the resource of a hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remarked: By consolidating army camps we have reduced personnel by more than four thousand — the equivalent of resources for a hundred thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 儻訓練精勇，人得其用，不惟勝敵，亦以省財。

translations.literal: If training makes them elite and brave, and each man finds his use, not only will they defeat the enemy, but finances will also be saved.
translations.idiomatic: If training makes them elite and each man is used to his full capacity, we will not only defeat our enemies but also save state revenue.

sentences.zh: ”安石等曰：“陛下頻年選擇使臣，專務訓練，間禦便殿躬親試閱，賞罰既明，士卒皆奮。

translations.literal: An Shi and others said: Your Majesty in successive years has selected envoys, devoted exclusively to training, and occasionally received them at the informal hall for personal testing and review; rewards and punishments being clear, all soldiers strive.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi and others replied: Your Majesty has for years appointed dedicated training officers and occasionally reviewed troops personally in the informal hall. With rewards and punishments clearly enforced, every soldier strives to excel.

sentences.zh: 觀其技藝之精，一人為數夫之敵，此實國家安危所係也。

translations.literal: Observing the fineness of their skills, one man is the match of several husbands; this truly bears on the state's security and peril.
translations.idiomatic: When their skills are honed, one soldier can match several ordinary men. This truly bears on the security of the state.

sentences.zh: ”是時，帝初置內教法，旬一禦便殿閱武，校程其能否而勸沮之，士無不爭勸者。

translations.literal: At this time, the emperor first established inner-court teaching methods; every ten days he received troops at the informal hall to review martial arts, gauging their ability and encouraging or restraining them; no soldier failed to strive.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor instituted the inner-court drill system, reviewing troops in the informal hall every ten days, assessing their ability and encouraging or restraining them as appropriate. No soldier failed to strive for excellence.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔教閱戰法，主將度地之形，隨宜施行。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict on instruction-review battle methods [said] the commanding general gauges the terrain's form and applies [methods] as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1074, an edict on instruction-review battle methods directed commanding generals to adapt tactics to the terrain.

sentences.zh: 二月，詔：“自今歲一遣使，按視五路安撫使以下及提舉教閱諸軍、義勇、保甲官，課其優劣以聞而誅賞之。

translations.literal: In the second month, an edict said: From this year one envoy is dispatched annually to inspect the five circuits' pacification commissioners and below, and officials supervising instruction-review of all armies, militia, and baojia, assessing their excellence and inferiority to report and punish or reward.
translations.idiomatic: In February, an edict declared: Beginning this year, an envoy shall be dispatched annually to inspect pacification commissioners and all officials responsible for drill review of armies, militia, and baojia units across the five circuits, assess their performance, and recommend rewards or punishments.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔：“在京諸軍營屯迫隘，馬無所調習。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict said: All army camps garrisoned in the capital are cramped and narrow; horses have nowhere to be drilled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1075, an edict noted: Army camps in the capital are too cramped for cavalry drill.

sentences.zh: 比創四教場，益寬大，可以馳騁。

translations.literal: Recently four drill grounds were created, more spacious and broad, where one can gallop freely.
translations.idiomatic: Four new drill grounds have been established, spacious enough for full galloping exercises.

sentences.zh: 其令騎軍就教者，日輪一營，以馬走驟閱習。

translations.literal: Those ordered cavalry to come for instruction: one camp per day in rotation, drilling with horses at running gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry units assigned to drill shall rotate one camp per day for mounted galloping exercises.

sentences.zh: ”五月，臧景陳馬射六事：一、順騣直射，二、背射，三、盤馬射，四、射親，五、野戰，六、輪弄，各為說以曉射者。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Zang Jing presented six matters of mounted archery: first, shooting straight along the horse's mane; second, shooting backward; third, shooting while wheeling the horse; fourth, close-range shooting; fifth, field battle; sixth, wheeling maneuvers — each with an explanation to instruct archers.
translations.idiomatic: In May, Zang Jing presented six mounted archery techniques: shooting along the horse's neck, backward shooting, shooting while wheeling, close-range shooting, field combat shooting, and wheeling maneuvers — each explained in detail for the instruction of archers.

sentences.zh: 詔依此教習。

translations.literal: An edict ordered training according to this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered training conducted according to these methods.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝令曾孝寬視教營陣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the emperor ordered Zeng Xiaokuan to observe teaching of camp formations.
translations.idiomatic: In August, the emperor ordered Zeng Xiaokuan to observe formation drill.

sentences.zh: 大閱八軍陣於荊家陂，訖事大賞。

translations.literal: A great review of the eight armies' formations was held at Jingjiapo; when finished, great rewards were given.
translations.idiomatic: A grand review of the eight armies' formations was held at Jingjiapo, followed by generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 元豐元年十月，詔立在京校試諸軍技藝格，第為上中下三等。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yuanfeng, an edict established standards for testing all armies' skills in the capital, ranked as upper, middle, and lower three grades.
translations.idiomatic: In October 1078, an edict established capital-wide standards for testing troops' martial skills, divided into upper, middle, and lower grades.

sentences.zh: 步射，六發而三中為一等，二中為二等，一中為三等。

translations.literal: Foot archery: six shots with three hits was first grade, two hits second grade, one hit third grade.
translations.idiomatic: For foot archery, three hits out of six shots qualified for the first grade, two hits for the second, and one hit for the third.

sentences.zh: 馬射，五發驟馬直射三矢、背射二矢，中數、等如步射法。

translations.literal: Mounted archery: five shots with galloping horse, three arrows shot straight and two shot backward; number of hits and grades followed the foot archery method.
translations.idiomatic: For mounted archery, five shots were required: three while galloping straight and two backward. Hit counts and grade assignments followed the foot archery rules.

sentences.zh: 弩射，自六中至二中，床子弩及炮自三中至一中，為及等。

translations.literal: Crossbow shooting: from six hits to two hits; bed-frame crossbow and catapult from three hits to one hit — these qualified for the grade.
translations.idiomatic: For crossbow shooting, six hits down to two qualified; for bed-frame crossbows and catapults, three hits down to one qualified.

sentences.zh: 並賞銀有差。

translations.literal: All received differentiated silver rewards.
translations.idiomatic: All qualified performers received graded silver rewards.

sentences.zh: 槍刀並標排手角勝負，計所勝第賞。

translations.literal: Spear, saber, and shield-bearers with standards competed for victory and defeat; rewards were ranked according to victories won.
translations.idiomatic: Spearmen, sabermen, and shield-bearers competed in paired contests, with rewards graded according to victories won.

sentences.zh: 其弓弩墜落，或縱矢不及堋，或挽弓破體，或局而不張，或矢不滿，或弩蹠不上牙，或擭不發，或身倒足落，並為不合格。

translations.literal: If bow or crossbow fell, or arrow released did not reach the butt, or drawing the bow broke the body, or the crossbow was set but not drawn, or arrow did not seat fully, or crossbow foot-stomp did not reach the trigger, or catch did not release, or body fell and feet dropped — all were unqualified.
translations.idiomatic: Dropping the bow or crossbow, failing to reach the target butt, breaking form while drawing, setting but not drawing the crossbow, failing to seat the arrow fully, failing to stomp the crossbow trigger, failing to release the catch, or falling from one's mount all counted as disqualification.

sentences.zh: 即射已中賞，餘箭不合格者，降一等，無可降者罷之。

translations.literal: Even if shooting had already earned a reward, if remaining arrows were unqualified, [the grade] was lowered one rank; if no rank remained to lower, [the soldier] was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Even if earlier shots had earned a reward, any subsequent unqualified shot lowered the grade by one rank; if no lower grade remained, the soldier was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 是月，賈逵、燕達等言：“近者增損東南排弩隊法，與東南所用兵械不同，請止依東南隊法，以弩手代小排。

translations.literal: That month, Jia Kui, Yan Da, and others said: Recently the southeast shield-crossbow squad method was increased and reduced, differing from weapons used in the southeast; they requested only following the southeast squad method, substituting crossbowmen for small shields.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Jia Kui, Yan Da, and others reported: Recent modifications to the southeast shield-crossbow squad method differ from weapons actually used in the southeast. We ask that only the original southeast squad method be followed, with crossbowmen replacing the small shield unit.

sentences.zh: 若去敵稍遠則施箭，近則左手持弩如小排架隔，右手執刀以備斬伐，與長兵相參為用。

translations.literal: If somewhat far from the enemy then shoot arrows; if near, the left hand holds the crossbow like a small shield to parry, the right hand holds a saber to prepare for cutting down, used together with long weapons.
translations.idiomatic: At greater distance they shoot; at close range the left hand holds the crossbow like a small shield for parrying while the right hand grips a saber for cutting, coordinated with long weapons.

sentences.zh: ”詔可，其槍手仍以標兼習。

translations.literal: The edict approved; spearmen were still to practice with standards concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal; spearmen were still required to practice with shield standards as well.

sentences.zh: 十一月，京西將劉元言：“馬軍教習不成，請降步軍，又不成，降廂軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Jingxi general Liu Yuanyan said: Cavalry who fail in instruction and practice, I request demotion to infantry; if again unsuccessful, demotion to garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: In November, Jingxi general Liu Yuanyan proposed: Cavalry who fail to master their drill should be demoted to infantry; if they fail again, to garrison troops.

sentences.zh: ”乃下令諸軍，約一季不能學者，如所請降之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an order was issued to all armies: those who within about one season could not learn, were demoted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: An order was then issued to all armies: any soldier who failed to master his assigned skills within one season would be demoted as proposed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔：“開封府界、京東西將兵，十人以一人習馬射，受教於中都所遣教頭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict: "For commanding troops in the Kaifeng prefectural boundary and the East and West Jing circuits, one man in ten shall practice mounted archery, receiving instruction from drill instructors dispatched from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered that among commanding troops in the Kaifeng prefectural boundary and the East and West Jing circuits, one soldier in ten was to train in mounted archery under drill instructors sent from the capital.

sentences.zh: 在京步軍諸營弓箭手，亦十人以一人習馬射，受教於教習馬軍所。

translations.literal: Among infantry archers of the various camps in the capital, likewise one man in ten shall practice mounted archery, receiving instruction from the office for training cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry archers in the capital's various camps were likewise required to have one man in ten train in mounted archery at the cavalry training office.

sentences.zh: 藝成，則展轉分教於其軍。

translations.literal: When their skill is complete, they shall in turn teach it throughout their army.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had mastered the skill, they were to teach it in rotation throughout their own units.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，遣內侍石得一閱視京西第五將所教馬軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, fourth month, the eunuch Shi Deyi was dispatched to inspect the cavalry being instructed by the Fifth Command of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year, the palace eunuch Shi Deyi was sent to review the cavalry under instruction by the Fifth Command of Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 五月，得一言其教習無狀，詔本將陳宗等具折。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Deyi reported that the instruction was improper; an edict ordered the commanders Chen Zong and others to submit detailed reports.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Deyi reported that drill standards had been grossly neglected. An edict required the unit commanders Chen Zong and his colleagues to submit full written accounts.

sentences.zh: 宗等引罪，帝責曰：“ 朝廷比以四方驕悍為可虞，選置將臣分總禁旅，俾時訓肄，以待非常。

translations.literal: Chen Zong and the others acknowledged guilt. The Emperor rebuked them, saying: "The court recently considered the arrogance and ferocity of the four directions worrisome, and selected and appointed generals to command the Imperial Guard in divisions, so that they would train on schedule in preparation for the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zong and the others pleaded guilty. The Emperor rebuked them: "The court has lately regarded the pride and violence of the frontier as a grave concern. We chose generals to command the Imperial Guard in separate divisions so they would drill on schedule and stand ready for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 至於部勒規模，悉經朕慮，前後告戒已極周詳。

translations.literal: As for organizational structure and regulations, all have passed through Our deliberation; warnings issued before and after have been extremely thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Every rule of command and every standard of drill has been weighed by Us personally. Our repeated admonitions could scarcely have been more explicit.

sentences.zh: 使宗等稍異木石，亦宜略知人意。

translations.literal: Even if Chen Zong and the others were somewhat unlike wood and stone, they should still have had some understanding of Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Even men less responsive than wood and stone ought to have grasped something of Our meaning.

sentences.zh: 屍祿日久，既頑且慵，苟遂矜寬，實難勵眾，可並勒停。

translations.literal: Drawing salaries for long without merit, they are both stubborn and lazy; if We now grant leniency, it will truly be hard to encourage the multitude. They are all to be suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: They have long lived off empty stipends, grown obstinate and slack. To show mercy now would make it impossible to rouse the ranks. All are to be dismissed from their posts.

sentences.zh: ”是月，詔殿前、步軍司兵各置都教頭掌隸教習之事，弩手五營、弓箭手十營、槍刀標排手五營各選一人武藝優者奏補。

translations.literal: " That month, an edict: The Palace Guard Bureau and Infantry Bureau shall each establish chief drill instructors to oversee instruction and training. From five camps of crossbowmen, ten camps of archers, and five camps of spearmen, sabermen, and shield-bearers, each shall select one man of superior martial skill and recommend him for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " That month, an edict directed the Palace Guard Bureau and the Infantry Bureau each to appoint chief drill instructors to supervise training. From five crossbow camps, ten archer camps, and five spear, saber, and shield camps, each was to nominate one soldier of outstanding skill for imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 逐司各舉散直二人為指使，罷巡教使臣。

translations.literal: Each bureau shall nominate two unattached-duty officers as directors, and the touring instruction commissioners shall be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau was to name two officers on detached duty as coordinators, and the touring drill commissioners were abolished.

sentences.zh: 是日，詔河東、陝西諸路：“舊制，馬軍自十月一日馳射野戰，至穀雨日止。

translations.literal: That same day, an edict to the circuits of Hedong and Shaanxi: "Under the old regulation, cavalry conducted galloping archery and field-combat training from the first day of the tenth month until Grain Rain.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, an edict went to the Hedong and Shaanxi circuits: "Under the former rule, cavalry trained in galloping archery and field combat from the first day of the tenth month until Grain Rain.

sentences.zh: 塞上地涼，自今教起八月，止五月一日。

translations.literal: On the frontier the land is cool; henceforth training shall begin in the eighth month and end on the first day of the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern frontier the climate is colder; henceforth drill is to begin in the eighth month and end on the first day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: ”七月，詔諸路教閱禁軍毋過兩時。

translations.literal: " In the seventh month, an edict: instruction-review drills for the Imperial Guard in all circuits shall not exceed two sessions.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventh month, an edict limited instruction-review drills for Imperial Guard units in every circuit to no more than two sessions per day.

sentences.zh: 九月，內出教法格並圖象頒行之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, training regulations and illustrated diagrams were issued from within the palace for promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the palace issued training regulations together with illustrated drill forms for distribution throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 步射執弓、發矢、運手、舉足、移步，及馬射、馬使蕃槍、馬上野戰格鬥，步用標排，皆有法象，凡千餘言，使軍士誦習焉。

translations.literal: For foot archery—holding the bow, loosing arrows, moving the hands, lifting the feet, and shifting steps—and for mounted archery, wielding foreign lances from horseback, and mounted field combat, and for infantry use of shields and standards—all had prescribed forms. In all more than a thousand characters, for soldiers to recite and practice.
translations.idiomatic: Foot archery—grip, release, hand movement, footwork, and stepping—and mounted archery, foreign lance work from horseback, mounted field fighting, and infantry shield-and-standard drill all had prescribed forms. The text ran to more than a thousand characters, which soldiers were to memorize and practice.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，詔東南諸路轉運、提點刑獄司，體量將兵自降教閱新法之後，軍士有所倍費以聞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, an edict to the transport commissioners and judicial inspection commissioners of the southeastern circuits: assess whether soldiers under commanding generals have incurred doubled expenses since the promulgation of the new instruction-review regulations, and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year, transport and judicial inspection commissioners in the southeast were ordered to investigate whether soldiers under regional commanders had faced doubled personal expenses since the new instruction-review regulations took effect, and to report their findings.

sentences.zh: 蓋自團立將兵以來，軍人日新教閱，舊資技藝以給私費者，悉無暇為故也。

translations.literal: This was because since the establishment of regional commands, soldiers drilled daily in instruction-review, and those who formerly relied on their skills to cover personal expenses had no time for it.
translations.idiomatic: The reason was that, once regional army commands were established, soldiers drilled in instruction-review every day. Men who had once used spare hours and side skills to meet private expenses no longer had the time.

sentences.zh: 六年，從郭忠紹之請，步軍弩手第一等者，令兼習神臂弓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, following Guo Zhongshao's request, first-grade infantry crossbowmen were ordered also to practice the Divine Arm bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, at Guo Zhongshao's request, first-tier infantry crossbowmen were ordered to train with the Divine Arm bow as well.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，詔開封府界、京東西路專選監司提舉教閱。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, an edict: specially select supervisory officials in the Kaifeng prefectural boundary and the East and West Jing circuits to oversee instruction-review drills.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventh year, an edict directed that supervisory officials be specially chosen in the Kaifeng prefectural boundary and the East and West Jing circuits to oversee instruction-review drills.

sentences.zh: 神宗留心武備，既命立武學、校《七書》以訓武舉之士，又頒兵法以肄軍旅，微妙淵通，取成於心，群臣莫望焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong paid close attention to military readiness. He ordered the establishment of the Martial Academy and collation of the Seven Military Classics to train candidates for military examinations, and also promulgated arts of war to drill the armies—subtle and profound, achieved from the heart—beyond what any minister could match.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong devoted himself to military preparedness. He founded the Martial Academy and had the Seven Military Classics collated to train military examination candidates, then promulgated battle doctrine to drill the armies—subtle, far-reaching, and shaped entirely by his own understanding, beyond anything his ministers could equal.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年四月，右司諫蘇轍上言：“諸道禁軍自置將以來，日夜按習武藝，將兵皆蚤晚兩教，新募之士或終日不得休息。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanyou, Right Remonstrance Bureau censor Su Zhe memorialized: "Since regional commanders were established for the Imperial Guard in all circuits, soldiers practice martial skills day and night. Commanding generals hold drills morning and evening, and newly recruited men sometimes get no rest all day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yuanyou, Right Remonstrance Bureau censor Su Zhe memorialized: "Since regional commanders were placed over the Imperial Guard in every circuit, troops have drilled in martial skills day and night. Commanders hold instruction morning and evening, and newly recruited men sometimes cannot rest from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 今平居無事，朝夕虐之以教閱，使無遺力以治生事，衣食殫盡，憔悴無聊，緩急安得其死力？

translations.literal: Now in peacetime, tormenting them morning and evening with instruction-review, leaving no strength for earning their livelihood—food and clothing exhausted, haggard and despondent—when urgency comes, how can one obtain their utmost devotion?
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times, when we grind them down morning and night with instruction-review, they have no strength left to make a living. Food and clothing run out; they grow gaunt and hopeless. When crisis comes, how can we expect them to fight to the death?

sentences.zh: 請使禁軍，除新募未習之人，其餘日止一教。

translations.literal: I request that for the Imperial Guard, except for newly recruited men not yet trained, the rest drill only once per day.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Imperial Guard, except for newly recruited men still in basic training, be limited to one drill session per day.

sentences.zh: 是月，朝請郎任公裕言：“軍中誦習新法，愚懵者頗以為苦。

translations.literal: That month, Court Gentleman Ren Gongyu said: "Reciting the new regulations in the army—the dull and confused find it quite burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Court Gentleman Ren Gongyu said: "Having the army memorize the new regulations has become a genuine hardship for slow-witted men.

sentences.zh: 夫射誌於中，而擊刺格鬥期於勝，豈必盡能如法？

translations.literal: Archery aims at hitting the mark; thrusting, striking, and combat aim at victory—must one fully perform according to every rule?
translations.idiomatic: Archery seeks to hit the target; thrusting and hand-to-hand fighting seek victory. Must every man reproduce the forms exactly?

sentences.zh: ”樞密院亦以為元降教閱新法自合教者指授，不當令兵眾例誦。

translations.literal: " The Bureau of Military Affairs also held that the instruction-review regulations originally promulgated ought to be taught by instructors through direct demonstration, and soldiers en masse should not be required to recite them.
translations.idiomatic: " The Bureau of Military Affairs agreed that the instruction-review regulations originally issued should be taught by drill instructors through direct demonstration, not recited in chorus by the rank and file.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 九月，樞密院奏：“異時馬軍教禦陣外，更教馬射。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized: "In former times, after cavalry drilled in defensive formations, they additionally trained in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Formerly, after cavalry finished defensive-formation drill, they also trained in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 其法：全隊馳馬皆重行為‘之’字，透空發矢，可迭出，最便利。

translations.literal: The method: the whole unit galloping in double lines forming a 'Zhi' character, loosing arrows through the air—they could emerge in rotation, most convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The method called for the entire unit to gallop in double ranks tracing a zigzag 'Zhi' pattern, loosing arrows into open air so that men could cycle out in turn. It was the most practical approach.

sentences.zh: 近歲專用順鬃直射、抹鞦背射法，止可輕騎挑戰，即用眾乃不能重列，非便。

translations.literal: In recent years they have relied exclusively on shooting straight along the mane and shooting backward by wiping the saddle bow—suitable only for light cavalry skirmishing; when deploying in force they cannot form double ranks—not convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years training has relied solely on shooting straight along the horse's mane and backward shots by sweeping the saddle bow—useful only for light cavalry skirmishes. In massed action the ranks cannot hold a double line. That is unsatisfactory.

sentences.zh: 請自今營閱排日，馬軍‘之’字射與立背射，隔日互教。

translations.literal: We request that from now on during camp review on scheduled days, cavalry alternate between 'Zhi'-pattern shooting and stationary backward shooting, teaching each on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that from now on, on scheduled camp-review days, cavalry alternate between zigzag-pattern shooting and stationary backward shooting, teaching one method one day and the other the next.

sentences.zh: ”詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，罷提舉教習馬軍所。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, the office for overseeing cavalry training was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, the office charged with supervising cavalry training was abolished.

sentences.zh: 六年六月，三衙申樞密院，乞近伏七十日依令式放諸軍教。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year, the Three Yamen petitioned the Bureau of Military Affairs, requesting that for the upcoming seventy-day dog-days period, all armies' drills be suspended according to regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the sixth year, the Three Yamen petitioned the Bureau of Military Affairs to suspend drill in all armies for the seventy-day dog-days period, as regulations prescribed.

sentences.zh: 王嚴叟白韓忠彥曰：“景德故事，皆內侍省檢舉傳宣，今但歲舉為常，則不復見朝廷恩意。

translations.literal: Wang Yansou informed Han Zhongyan: "Under the Jingde precedent, the Palace Domestic Service reported and announced it. If it is merely cited annually as routine, the court's gracious intent will no longer be visible.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yansou told Han Zhongyan: "Under the Jingde precedent, the Palace Domestic Service investigated the matter and issued the announcement. If we treat it as an annual routine, the court's gracious concern will no longer be felt.

sentences.zh: ”忠彥以為然，又開陳太皇太后。

translations.literal: " Han Zhongyan agreed, and also presented this to the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Zhongyan agreed and raised the point with the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 曰：“如此則為常事，待處分內侍省。

translations.literal: She said: "If so it becomes routine; wait for disposition of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: She said: "If it becomes an ordinary annual matter, let the Palace Domestic Service handle the arrangements.

sentences.zh: ”遂詔：“今後入伏，遣中侍傳宣諸軍住教。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict: "Henceforth when the dog days begin, eunuch attendants shall be dispatched to announce suspension of drill to all armies.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict followed: "Henceforth, when the dog days begin, eunuch attendants are to be sent to announce to all armies that drill is suspended.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年三月，樞密院言：“禁軍春秋大教賞法，每千人增取二百一十人，給賞有差。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Shaosheng, the Bureau of Military Affairs stated: "For Imperial Guard spring and autumn grand drill reward regulations, for every thousand men an additional two hundred and ten are selected; rewards vary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Shaosheng, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Under the spring and autumn grand drill reward rules for the Imperial Guard, two hundred and ten additional men are chosen for every thousand; rewards are graded accordingly.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，樞密院言：“馬軍自九月至三月，每十日一次出城氵率渲，教習回答野戰走驟向背施放，遇風雪假故權住。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, the Bureau of Military Affairs stated: "From the ninth month to the third month, cavalry shall once every ten days go outside the city for field drill, practicing responses for field combat, galloping charges, advancing and retreating, and shooting; in cases of wind, snow, or leave, training shall be temporarily suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "From the ninth month through the third month, cavalry are to leave the city once every ten days for field drill, training in field-combat responses, galloping maneuvers, advances and retreats, and shooting. Training may be temporarily suspended for wind, snow, or approved leave.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，詔在京、府界諸路禁軍格鬥法，自今並依元豐條法教習。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, an edict: combat methods for the Imperial Guard in the capital, the prefectural boundary, and all circuits shall henceforth all follow Yuanfeng regulations for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, an edict ordered that hand-to-hand combat methods for Imperial Guard units in the capital, the prefectural boundary, and all circuits were henceforth to follow Yuanfeng regulations.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔選弩手兼習神臂弓。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, an edict: select crossbowmen also to practice the Divine Arm bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, an edict directed that crossbowmen be selected to train with the Divine Arm bow as well.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔：“殿前、馬步軍司見管教頭，別選事藝精強、通曉教像體法者，展轉教習。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict: "Among the current drill instructors of the Palace Guard Bureau and the Cavalry and Infantry Bureaus, separately select men of refined skill who thoroughly understand the illustrated training methods, to teach in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, an edict ordered: "From among the Palace Guard Bureau's and the Cavalry and Infantry Bureaus' current drill instructors, select men of exceptional skill who fully understand the illustrated training forms, and have them teach in rotation.

sentences.zh: 其弓箭手馬、步射射親，用點藥包指及第二指知鏃，並如元豐格法。

translations.literal: For archers in mounted and foot close-range shooting, using the tip of the index finger and the second finger to feel the arrowhead—all as in Yuanfeng regulations.
translations.idiomatic: For archers in mounted and foot close-range shooting, the index fingertip and second finger are used to feel the arrowhead—all according to Yuanfeng regulations.

sentences.zh: ”是月，又詔復神臂弓射法為百二十步。

translations.literal: " That month, another edict restored the Divine Arm bow shooting method to one hundred twenty paces.
translations.idiomatic: " That month, another edict restored the Divine Arm bow shooting distance to one hundred twenty paces.

sentences.zh: 元符元年十月，曾布既上巡教使臣罰格，因言：“祖宗以來，禦將士常使恩歸人主，而威令在管軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yuanfu, Zeng Bu, having submitted penalty regulations for touring instruction commissioners, further stated: "Since the founding ancestors, in governing officers and soldiers grace has always been made to flow to the sovereign, while authority and commands rested with the commanding generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yuanfu, after submitting penalty regulations for touring drill commissioners, Zeng Bu added: "Since the founding of the dynasty, favor shown to officers and soldiers has always been made to reflect on the sovereign, while discipline and command have rested with the unit commanders.

sentences.zh: 凡申嚴軍政，豈待朝廷立法而後施行耶？

translations.literal: For enforcing military discipline—must one wait for the court to legislate before implementing?
translations.idiomatic: Must military discipline wait for the court to pass a law before it can be enforced?

sentences.zh: 是管軍失職矣。

translations.literal: This means the commanding generals have failed in duty.
translations.idiomatic: To require such legislation is itself a dereliction by the commanders.

sentences.zh: ”帝深以為然。

translations.literal: " The Emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 政和元年二月，詔：“春秋大教，諸軍弓弩鬥力，並依元豐舊制。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Zhenghe, an edict: "For spring and autumn grand drills, bow and crossbow draw-strength contests for all armies shall follow the old Yuanfeng system.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Zhenghe, an edict ordered: "In the spring and autumn grand drills, bow and crossbow draw-strength competitions for all armies shall follow the former Yuanfeng system.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，臣僚上言：“神臂弓垛遠百二十步，給箭十隻，取五中為合格，軍中少得該賞，恐惰於習射。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, officials memorialized: "For the Divine Arm bow at a stacked target one hundred twenty paces distant, ten arrows are given; five hits qualify. Few in the army merit rewards, and there is fear of neglect in practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year, officials memorialized: "With the Divine Arm bow at a stacked target one hundred twenty paces away, ten arrows are issued and five hits are required to qualify. Too few soldiers earn rewards, and practice may grow slack.

sentences.zh: 送殿前、馬步軍司勘會，將中貼箭數並改為上垛，其一中貼此兩上垛。

translations.literal: Refer to the Palace Guard Bureau and the Cavalry and Infantry Bureaus for investigation: change hits counted on the target face to upper-butts; one hit on the target face shall equal two upper-butts.
translations.idiomatic: Refer the matter to the Palace Guard Bureau and the Cavalry and Infantry Bureaus for review: count hits on the target face as upper-mound hits, with one target-face hit equal to two upper-mound hits.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，詔：“自今敢占留將兵，不赴教閱，並以違御筆論。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, an edict: "Henceforth anyone who dares detain commanding troops and fail to attend instruction-review shall be prosecuted as violating an imperial rescript.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, an edict declared: "Henceforth anyone who dares hold back commanding troops from instruction-review shall be punished for violating an imperial rescript.

sentences.zh: 不按舉者，如其罪。

translations.literal: Those who fail to report it shall share the same punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who fail to report such offenses shall be punished equally.

sentences.zh: ”十一月，臣僚言：“春秋大教，諸軍弓弩上取鬥力高強，其射親中多者，激賞太薄，無以為勸。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh month, officials stated: "For spring and autumn grand drills, bow and crossbow contests select those of highest draw strength, and those with many close-range hits—the incentive rewards are too meager, insufficient to encourage.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eleventh month, officials reported: "In the spring and autumn grand drills, bow and crossbow competitions reward the strongest draw and the most close-range hits, yet the incentive payments are too small to motivate the troops.

sentences.zh: ”詔依元豐法。

translations.literal: " An edict: follow Yuanfeng regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered a return to Yuanfeng regulations.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔州郡禁軍出戍外，常留五分在州教閱，從毛友之請也。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict: for Imperial Guard units in prefectures and commanderies deployed on external garrison duty, five-tenths shall permanently remain in the prefecture for instruction-review drill—following Mao You's request.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, at Mao You's request, an edict required that when prefectural Imperial Guard units were sent on external garrison duty, half the force was to remain in the prefecture for instruction-review drill.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年四月，立騎射賞法，其背射上垛中貼者，依步射法推賞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Xuanhe, mounted archery reward regulations were established; backward shooting hits on the upper mound or target face shall be rewarded according to the foot archery method.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Xuanhe, reward rules for mounted archery were established: backward shots that hit the upper mound or the target face were to be rewarded by the same standards used for foot archery.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年二月，詔：“軍兵久失教習，當汰冗濫。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Jingkang, an edict: "Soldiers have long lacked training and must be winnowed of redundancy and lax standards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Jingkang, an edict declared: "The army has long gone without proper drill and must be purged of slack and redundant men.

sentences.zh: 今三衙與諸將招軍，惟務增數希賞，但及等杖，不問勇怯。

translations.literal: Now the Three Yamen and various generals recruit soldiers, seeking only to increase numbers for rewards; so long as the height standard is met, courage and timidity are not asked.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Three Yamen and regional generals recruit solely to inflate numbers and claim rewards. So long as a man meets the height requirement, no one asks whether he is brave or timid.

sentences.zh: 招收既不精當，教習又不以時，雜色占破，十居三四。

translations.literal: Recruitment is neither refined nor proper; training is not timely; miscellaneous duties occupy them—three or four in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Recruitment is careless, training irregular, and miscellaneous assignments consume the men—three or four out of every ten.

sentences.zh: 今宜招兵之際，精加揀擇，既係軍籍，專使教習，不得以雜色拘占。

translations.literal: Now at recruitment one should carefully select; once on the rolls, dedicate them to training; they must not be detained for miscellaneous duties.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits should be carefully chosen. Once enrolled, they should train exclusively and must not be pulled away for miscellaneous duties.

sentences.zh: 又神臂弓、馬黃弩乃中國長技，宜多行教習，以扞邊騎。

translations.literal: Moreover the Divine Arm bow and the locust crossbow are China's supreme skills; training should be widely conducted to resist frontier cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Arm bow and the locust crossbow are among the empire's finest weapons. They should be taught widely to counter enemy horsemen on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 仍令間用衣甲教閱，庶使習熟。

translations.literal: Also order periodic instruction-review drills in armor, so they may grow practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Drill should also be conducted periodically in armor so that men grow accustomed to fighting in full kit.

sentences.zh: ” 四月，詔復置教場，春秋大閱，及復內教法以激賞之。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month, an edict reestablished drill grounds, spring and autumn grand reviews, and restored inner-court training methods to motivate with rewards.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fourth month, an edict reestablished drill grounds, restored spring and autumn grand reviews, and revived palace training standards backed by reward incentives.

sentences.zh: 陣法熙寧二年十一月，趙禼乞講求諸葛亮八陣法，以授邊將，使之應變。

translations.literal: Battle formations. In the eleventh month of the second year of Xining, Zhao Xu requested to study Zhuge Liang's Eight Formations method to teach frontier generals, enabling them to adapt.
translations.idiomatic: Battle Formations. In the eleventh month of the second year of Xining, Zhao Xu asked to investigate Zhuge Liang's Eight Formations and teach them to frontier generals so they could respond to changing conditions.

sentences.zh: 詔郭逵同禼講求，相度地形，定為陣圖聞奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guo Kui to join Xu in the study, assess terrain, fix the formation diagrams, and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Guo Kui to join Zhao Xu in the investigation, survey the terrain, finalize formation diagrams, and submit a memorial.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，詔蔡挺先進教閱陣圖。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifth year, an edict for Cai Ting to submit instruction-review formation diagrams first.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year, an edict required Cai Ting to submit instruction-review formation diagrams in advance.

sentences.zh: 帝嚐謂：“今之邊臣無知奇正之體者，況奇正之變乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "Today's frontier officials know nothing of the substance of orthodox and unorthodox formations—how much less their transformations!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once remarked: "Our frontier commanders today understand neither the basic principles of orthodox and unorthodox formations, nor—what is harder still—their transformations.

sentences.zh: 且天地五行之數不過五，五陣之變，出於自然，非強為之。

translations.literal: Moreover the numbers of Heaven and Earth and the Five Phases do not exceed five; the transformations of the five formations arise from nature, not forced artifice.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, earth, and the Five Phases never exceed the number five. The variations of the five formations arise from nature; they are not arbitrary inventions.

sentences.zh: ”宰相韓絳因請諸帥臣各具戰陣之法來上，取其所長，立以為法。

translations.literal: " Chancellor Han Jiang thereupon requested all frontier commanders each submit their battle formation methods, take the best, and establish them as law.
translations.idiomatic: " Chancellor Han Jiang then asked every frontier commander to submit his own battle-formation methods so the court could adopt the best and codify them.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 帝患諸將軍行無行陣之法，嚐曰：“李靖結三人為隊必有意。

translations.literal: The Emperor worried that generals on campaign had no marching formation methods, and once said: "Li Jing's forming three men into a squad must have had a reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was troubled that campaigning generals had no marching-formation doctrine and once said: "When Li Jing grouped three men into a squad, he must have had a purpose.

sentences.zh: 星書，羽林皆以三人為隊，靖深曉此，非無據也。

translations.literal: In star lore, the Feathered Forest all use three men per squad—Jing deeply understood this, not without basis.
translations.idiomatic: In astrological writings, the Feathered Forest constellation is arrayed in threes. Li Jing understood that deeply; his method was not groundless.

sentences.zh: ”乃令賈逵、郭固試之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Jia Kui and Guo Gu to test it.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Jia Kui and Guo Gu to trial the method.

sentences.zh: 十二月，知通遠軍王韶請降合行條約，詔賜御製《攻守圖》、《行軍環珠》、《武經總要》、《神武秘略》、《風角集占》、《四路戰守約束》各一部，餘令關秦鳳路經略司抄錄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Administrator of Tongyuan Army Wang Shao requested decrees on regulations to be enforced. An edict granted one copy each of the imperially compiled Attack and Defense Diagrams, Marching Ring-Pearl, Essentials of the Military Canon, Secret Strategies of Divine Warfare, Collected Wind-Omen Divinations, and Four-Circuit Battle-and-Defense Regulations; the remainder to be copied by the Qinfeng Circuit Frontier Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Wang Shao, administrator of Tongyuan Army, requested copies of regulations in force. An edict granted him one copy each of the imperial Attack and Defense Diagrams, Marching Ring-Pearl, Essentials of the Military Canon, Secret Strategies of Divine Warfare, Collected Wind-Omen Divinations, and Four-Circuit Battle-and-Defense Regulations; other titles were to be copied by the Qinfeng Circuit frontier commission.

sentences.zh: 六年，詔諸路經略司，結隊並依李靖法，三人為一小隊，九人為一中隊，賞罰俟成序日取裁。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, an edict to all circuit frontier commissions: squad formation all according to Li Jing's method—three men as a small squad, nine as a medium squad; rewards and punishments to be determined once order is established.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, an edict to every circuit frontier commission required squad organization to follow Li Jing's method: three men to a small squad, nine to a medium squad. Rewards and punishments were to be fixed once the system was in order.

sentences.zh: 其隊伍及器甲之數，依涇原路牙教法。

translations.literal: Numbers of squads and armor to follow the Jingyuan Circuit training-teeth method.
translations.idiomatic: Squad counts and armor allotments were to follow the Jingyuan Circuit drill-teeth regulations.

sentences.zh: 九月，趙禼言：“欲自今大閱漢蕃陣隊，且以萬二千五百人為法，旌旗麾幟各隨方色。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhao Xu said: "I wish from now in grand reviews of Han and non-Han formation units to take twelve thousand five hundred men as the standard; banners and pennants each following directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Zhao Xu proposed: "In future grand reviews of Han and non-Han formation units, I propose a standard force of twelve thousand five hundred men, with banners and pennants colored according to the cardinal directions.

sentences.zh: 戰國時，大將之旗以龜為飾，蓋取前列先知之義。

translations.literal: In Warring States times, the great general's banner was ornamented with a tortoise—taking the meaning of the vanguard knowing first.
translations.idiomatic: In Warring States times a field commander's banner bore the tortoise emblem, signifying that the vanguard must see ahead of all others.

sentences.zh: 令中軍亦宜以龜為號。

translations.literal: Now the central army should also take the tortoise as its sign.
translations.idiomatic: The central army should likewise adopt the tortoise as its emblem.

sentences.zh: 其八隊旗，別繪天、地、風、雲、龍、虎、鳥、蛇。

translations.literal: Its eight unit banners should separately depict Heaven, Earth, Wind, Cloud, Dragon, Tiger, Bird, and Serpent.
translations.idiomatic: The eight unit banners should be painted with Heaven, Earth, Wind, Cloud, Dragon, Tiger, Bird, and Serpent.

sentences.zh: 天、地則象其方園，風、雲則狀其飛揚，龍、虎則狀其猛厲，鳥、蛇則狀其翔盤之勢，以備大閱。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth would represent their square and round forms; Wind and Cloud their soaring movement; Dragon and Tiger their fierce power; Bird and Serpent their circling flight—for grand review.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth would show square and round forms; Wind and Cloud their rising motion; Dragon and Tiger their fierce power; Bird and Serpent their wheeling flight—all for the grand review.

sentences.zh: ”樞密院以為陣隊旗號若繪八物，應士眾難辨，且其間亦有無形可繪者。

translations.literal: " The Bureau of Military Affairs held that if formation unit banners painted the eight creatures, soldiers would be hard-pressed to distinguish them, and among them some have no visible form to paint.
translations.idiomatic: " The Bureau of Military Affairs objected that if formation banners depicted all eight symbols, troops would struggle to tell them apart, and some symbols have no fixed shape that can be painted.

sentences.zh: 遂詔止依方色，仍異其形製，令勿雜而已。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict: only follow directional colors, yet vary their shapes and forms, ordering they not be confused—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: banners were to use directional colors only, with distinct shapes so units would not be confused—and no more.

sentences.zh: 七年，又命呂惠卿、曾孝寬比校三五結隊法。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Lü Huiqing and Zeng Xiaokuan were additionally ordered to compare the three-five squad-formation methods.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Lü Huiqing and Zeng Xiaokuan were ordered to compare the three-five squad-formation methods.

sentences.zh: 十月，以新定結隊法並賞罰格及置陣形勢等，遣近侍李憲付趙禼曰：“陣法之詳已令憲麵諭，今所圖止是一小陣，卿其從容析問，憲必一一有說。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the newly fixed squad-formation method together with reward-and-penalty regulations and deployment formation layouts, etc., were sent by palace attendant Li Xian to Zhao Xu, saying: "The details of formation method have been orally explained to you by Li Xian; the diagram now submitted is only one small formation—you should calmly analyze and inquire; Xian will have an explanation for each point.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, palace attendant Li Xian delivered the newly fixed squad-formation method, reward-and-penalty regulations, and deployment diagrams to Zhao Xu with this message: "Li Xian has already explained the formation doctrine to you in person. The diagram provided shows only one small formation. Question him at leisure; he can answer every point.

sentences.zh: 然置陣法度，久失其傳，今朕一旦據意所得，率爾為法，恐有未盡，宜無避忌，但具奏來。

translations.literal: However, deployment formation regulations have long lost their transmission; now We have suddenly taken what We grasped from Our own understanding and hastily made it law—We fear there are inadequacies. You should not hold back—simply memorialize fully.
translations.idiomatic: Deployment doctrine has long been lost. We have now improvised a system from Our own understanding and set it down hastily as law. We fear it is incomplete. Speak without reserve and report everything in full.

sentences.zh: ”繼又詔曰：“近令李憲齎新定結隊法並賞罰格付卿，同議可否，因以團立將官，更置陣法，卿必深悉朝廷經畫之意。
