translations.literal: " A subsequent edict said: "Recently We ordered Li Xian to deliver the newly fixed squad method and reward-and-penalty regulations to you, to discuss together whether they are feasible; in connection with establishing regional commanders and reforming deployment formations—you must deeply understand the court's strategic intent.
translations.idiomatic: " A follow-up edict read: "We recently sent Li Xian to deliver the new squad-formation method and reward-and-penalty regulations for your joint review. This work accompanies the establishment of regional commanders and the reform of battle formations. You must grasp the court's strategic purpose fully.

sentences.zh: 如日近可了，宜令李憲齎赴闕。

translations.literal: If it can be completed soon, Li Xian should be ordered to bring them to court.
translations.idiomatic: If the review can be finished soon, have Li Xian bring the materials to court.

sentences.zh: ”禼奏曰：

translations.literal: " Zhao Xu memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Xu replied in memorial:

sentences.zh: 置陣之法，以結隊為先。

translations.literal: The method of deployment formation takes squad formation as primary.
translations.idiomatic: In deployment doctrine, squad organization comes first.

sentences.zh: 李靖以五十人為一隊，每三人自相得者結為一小隊，合三小隊為一中隊，合五中隊為一大隊，餘押官、隊頭、副隊頭、左右傔旗五人即充五十，並相依附。

translations.literal: Li Jing took fifty men as one squad; every three who found one another compatible formed a small squad; three small squads combined as one medium squad; five medium squads combined as one large squad; the remaining five—supervisory officer, squad leader, deputy squad leader, and left and right adjutant-banner men—making fifty in all, all mutually attached.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing made fifty men one squad. Every three compatible men formed a small squad; three small squads formed a medium squad; five medium squads formed a large squad. The remaining five—the supervisory officer, squad leader, deputy leader, and left and right adjutant-banner men—brought the total to fifty, all bound to one another.

sentences.zh: 今聖製：每一大隊合五中隊，五十人為之；

translations.literal: Now the imperial regulations: each large squad combines five medium squads, fifty men making one;
translations.idiomatic: Under the imperial regulations now in force, each large squad comprises five medium squads, fifty men in all;

sentences.zh: 中隊合三小隊，九人為之；

translations.literal: Each medium squad combines three small squads, nine men making one;
translations.idiomatic: each medium squad comprises three small squads of nine men;

sentences.zh: 小隊合三人為之，亦擇心意相得者。

translations.literal: Each small squad combines three men, likewise selecting those compatible in mind and will.
translations.idiomatic: and each small squad is three men chosen for mutual trust and compatibility.

sentences.zh: 又選壯勇善槍者一人為旗頭，令自擇如己藝、心相得者二人為左右傔；

translations.literal: Further, one strong and brave man skilled with the spear is chosen as flag leader, and ordered to select for himself two men of like skill and mutual compatibility as left and right adjutants;
translations.idiomatic: One stalwart skilled with the spear is chosen as flag leader and allowed to pick two men of comparable skill and temperament as his left and right adjutants;

sentences.zh: 次選勇悍者一人為引戰；

translations.literal: Next one fierce and bold man is chosen as battle initiator;
translations.idiomatic: next a fierce fighter is chosen as vanguard;

sentences.zh: 又選軍校一人執刀在後，為擁隊。

translations.literal: Further one military officer is chosen to hold a blade in the rear as rally guard.
translations.idiomatic: and one military officer with drawn blade is posted to the rear as rally guard.

sentences.zh: 凡隊內一人用命，二人應援；

translations.literal: In general, within the squad when one man fights to the death, two men provide support;
translations.idiomatic: Within every squad, when one man goes all out, two must support him;

sentences.zh: 小隊用命，中隊應援；

translations.literal: When the small squad fights to the death, the medium squad provides support;
translations.idiomatic: when a small squad is committed, the medium squad must respond;

sentences.zh: 中隊用命，大隊應援；

translations.literal: When the medium squad fights to the death, the large squad provides support;
translations.idiomatic: when a medium squad is committed, the large squad must respond;

sentences.zh: 大隊用命，小隊應援。

translations.literal: When the large squad fights to the death, the small squads provide support.
translations.idiomatic: When the large squad is committed, the small squads must respond in turn.

sentences.zh: 如逗撓觀望不即赴救，致有陷失者，本隊委擁隊軍校，次隊委本轄隊將，審觀不救所由，斬之。

translations.literal: If through hesitation and watching one does not immediately go to the rescue, causing defeat and loss, the rally-guard military officer of the squad in question is entrusted with the case, and the squad commander of the next squad with jurisdiction is entrusted; they are to examine the reason for not rescuing and behead the offender.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who hangs back or waits instead of rushing to the rescue, thereby causing defeat or loss, shall be investigated by the rally-guard officer of his own squad and the commander of the next squad in the chain; once the reason for failure to rescue is established, the offender is to be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 其有不可救，或赴救不及，或身自受敵，體被重創，但非可救者，皆不坐。

translations.literal: Those cases where rescue was impossible, or rescue could not arrive in time, or one personally received the enemy and the body suffered grave wounds—provided rescue was genuinely impossible—none are held liable.
translations.idiomatic: No penalty applies where rescue was impossible, where help could not arrive in time, or where a man was himself under heavy attack and gravely wounded—provided the situation was truly beyond rescue.

sentences.zh: 其說雖與古同，而用法尤為精密。

translations.literal: Although the doctrine is the same as antiquity, its application is especially precise.
translations.idiomatic: The doctrine matches the ancients, but its application is far more exact.

sentences.zh: 此蓋陛下天錫勇智，不學而能也。

translations.literal: This is surely because Your Majesty was heaven-endowed with courage and wisdom, able without study.
translations.idiomatic: This surely reflects courage and wisdom heaven-bestowed upon Your Majesty— mastery without need of study.

sentences.zh: 然議者謂四十五人而一長，不若五人而一長之密。

translations.literal: Yet critics say one leader for forty-five men is not as tight as one leader for five men.
translations.idiomatic: Critics object, however, that one leader for every forty-five men is less tight than one for every five.

sentences.zh: 且以五人而一長，即五十人而十長也，推之於百千萬，則為長者多，而統製不一也。

translations.literal: Moreover, with one leader for five men, that is ten leaders for fifty men; extended to hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands, leaders become numerous and unified command is lost.
translations.idiomatic: One leader per five men means ten leaders for fifty; carried to hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands, leaders multiply and unified command breaks down.

sentences.zh: 至如周製：五人為伍，屬之比長；

translations.literal: As for the Zhou system: five men made a squad, subordinate to a squad chief;
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Zhou system: five men formed a squad under a squad chief;

sentences.zh: 五伍為兩，屬之閭胥；

translations.literal: five squads made a pair, subordinate to a neighborhood clerk;
translations.idiomatic: five squads formed a pair under a neighborhood clerk;

sentences.zh: 四兩為卒，屬之族師；

translations.literal: four pairs made a platoon, subordinate to a clan instructor;
translations.idiomatic: four pairs formed a platoon under a clan instructor;

sentences.zh: 五卒為旅，屬之黨正；

translations.literal: five platoons made a company, subordinate to a precinct chief;
translations.idiomatic: five platoons formed a company under a precinct chief;

sentences.zh: 五旅為師，屬之州長；

translations.literal: five companies made a division, subordinate to a prefectural chief;
translations.idiomatic: five companies formed a division under a prefectural chief;

sentences.zh: 五師為軍，屬之命卿。

translations.literal: five divisions made an army, subordinate to an appointed minister.
translations.idiomatic: five divisions formed an army under an appointed minister.

sentences.zh: 此猶今之軍製，百人為都，五都為營，五營為軍，十軍為廂。

translations.literal: This is like today's military system: one hundred men make a company, five companies a battalion, five battalions an army, ten armies a wing.
translations.idiomatic: This parallels the present military organization: one hundred men to a company, five companies to a battalion, five battalions to an army, and ten armies to a wing.

sentences.zh: 自廂都指揮使而下，各有節級，有員品，亦昔之比長、閭胥、族師、黨正之任也。

translations.literal: From wing commander downward, each has rank and grade and authorized posts—the same duties as the ancient squad chief, neighborhood clerk, clan instructor, and precinct chief.
translations.idiomatic: From the wing commander down, every rank has its grade and authorized strength—the same functions once held by squad chiefs, neighborhood clerks, clan instructors, and precinct chiefs.

sentences.zh: 議者謂什伍之製，於都法為便，然都法恐非臨陣對敵決勝之術也。

translations.literal: Critics say the decimal-and-five-squad system is convenient for company regulations, yet company regulations are probably not the art of facing the enemy in battle array and deciding victory.
translations.idiomatic: Critics hold that the decimal-and-five-squad system suits company drill well enough, but company drill is hardly the art of meeting the enemy in battle and winning.

sentences.zh: 況八陣之法，久失其傳，聖製一新，稽之前聞，若合符節。

translations.literal: Moreover, the method of the eight formations had long lost its transmission; the imperial regulations newly set forth, checked against earlier accounts, match like tally and seal.
translations.idiomatic: The eight-formation doctrine had long been lost; Your Majesty's new system, compared with earlier accounts, fits them like tally to seal.

sentences.zh: 夫法一定，易以致人。

translations.literal: When a method is fixed, it is easy for the enemy to manipulate one.
translations.idiomatic: Once a formation is fixed, the enemy can easily manipulate you.

sentences.zh: 敵好擊虛，吾以虛形之；

translations.literal: The enemy likes to strike the empty; we show them the empty;
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy likes to strike where we seem weak, we show weakness;

sentences.zh: 敵好背實，吾以實形之。

translations.literal: The enemy likes to turn from the solid; we show them the solid.
translations.idiomatic: if he likes to turn away from strength, we show strength.

sentences.zh: 然而所擊者非其虛，所背者非其實，故逸能勞之，飽能饑之，此所謂致人而不致於人也。

translations.literal: Yet what is struck is not truly empty, and what is turned from is not truly solid; thus the rested can be wearied and the full can be starved—this is what is called making others come to you without your going to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what he strikes is not truly weak, and what he turns from is not truly strong—so the rested enemy can be worn down and the fed enemy can be starved. This is what it means to move the enemy without being moved by him.

sentences.zh: 七年七月，詔諸路安撫使各具可用陣隊法，及訪求知陣隊法者以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, seventh month, an edict ordered the pacification commissioners of each circuit each to submit usable squad-and-formation methods, and to seek out and report persons who knew squad-and-formation methods.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, seventh month, an edict directed every circuit pacification commissioner to submit workable squad-and-formation methods and to seek out and report anyone versed in such doctrine.

sentences.zh: 九月，崇儀使郭固以同詳定古今陣法賜對，於是內出《攻守圖》二十五部付河北。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Honored Ceremonial Commissioner Guo Gu was granted audience for jointly examining and fixing ancient and modern formation methods; thereupon twenty-five copies of Attack-and-Defense Diagrams were issued from within and sent to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Honored Ceremonial Commissioner Guo Gu was granted audience for his work jointly codifying ancient and modern formations; the court then issued twenty-five copies of the Attack-and-Defense Diagrams to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 八年二月，帝批：“見校試七軍營陣，以分數不齊，前後抵牾，難為施用。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, second month, the emperor annotated: "The seven-army camp formations now being tested in review, because the troop counts are uneven and front and rear contradict one another, are hard to apply.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, second month, the emperor wrote in the margin: "The seven-army camp formations under review have uneven troop strengths and conflicting front-and-rear arrangements, making them hard to use.

sentences.zh: 可令見校試官摭其可取者，草定八軍法以聞。

translations.literal: The officials now conducting the review may be ordered to gather what is usable and draft an eight-army method for report.
translations.idiomatic: Order the review officers to gather what is workable and draft an eight-army method for submission.

sentences.zh: ”初，詔樞密院曰：“唐李靖兵法，世無全書，雜見《通典》，離析訛舛。

translations.literal: " Earlier, an edict to the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Tang Li Jing's military methods have no complete book in the world; they appear scattered in the Comprehensive Institutions, broken apart and erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier an edict to the Bureau of Military Affairs had said: "Li Jing's Tang military treatise survives only in fragments scattered through the Comprehensive Institutions, disjointed and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 又官號物名與今稱謂不同，武人將佐多不能通其意。

translations.literal: Moreover, official titles and object names differ from present usage, and military officers and aides mostly cannot grasp their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Official titles and equipment names differ from present usage, and most officers and aides cannot make sense of them.

sentences.zh: 令樞密院檢詳官與王震、曾收、王白、郭逢原等校正，分類解釋，令今可行。

translations.literal: Let the Bureau of Military Affairs review officers together with Wang Zhen, Zeng Shou, Wang Bai, Guo Fengyuan, and others collate and correct them, classify and explain them, and make them practicable for the present.
translations.idiomatic: Have the bureau's review officers, together with Wang Zhen, Zeng Shou, Wang Bai, Guo Fengyuan, and others, collate, classify, and explain the text so that it can be put into practice today.

sentences.zh: ”又命樞密院副都承旨張誠一、入內押班李憲與震、逢原行視寬廣處，用馬步軍二千八百人教李靖營陣法。

translations.literal: " Further, Vice Director of Palace Reception Zhang Chengyi of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Inner-Palace Escort Chief Li Xian, together with Zhen and Fengyuan, were ordered to go inspect open ground and, using two thousand eight hundred mounted and foot troops, teach Li Jing's camp formation method.
translations.idiomatic: " The court also ordered Vice Director of Palace Reception Zhang Chengyi of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Inner-Palace Escort Chief Li Xian, together with Wang Zhen and Guo Fengyuan, to find open ground and drill two thousand eight hundred mounted and foot soldiers in Li Jing's camp-formation method.

sentences.zh: 以步軍副都指揮使楊遂為都大提舉，誠一、憲為同提舉，震、逢原參議公事，夏元象、臧景等為將副、部隊將、幹當公事，凡三十九人。

translations.literal: Foot Army Vice Commander-in-Chief Yang Sui was made chief superintendent; Chengyi and Xian were made co-superintendents; Zhen and Fengyuan were made planning officers; Xia Yuanxiang, Zang Jing, and others served as deputy generals, troop squad commanders, and staff officers—in all thirty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: Foot Army Vice Commander-in-Chief Yang Sui was appointed chief superintendent; Zhang Chengyi and Li Xian were co-superintendents; Wang Zhen and Guo Fengyuan were planning officers; Xia Yuanxiang, Zang Jing, and others served as deputy generals, troop squad commanders, and staff officers—thirty-nine men in all.

sentences.zh: 誠一等初用李靖六花陣法，約受兵二萬人為率，為七軍，內虞候軍各二千八百人，取戰兵千九百人為七十六隊，戰兵內每軍弩手三百，弓手三百，馬軍五百，跳蕩四百，奇兵四百，輜重每軍九百，是為二千八百人。

translations.literal: Chengyi and the others at first used Li Jing's six-flower formation method, taking roughly twenty thousand accepted troops as the standard, forming seven armies; within this each rear-guard army had two thousand eight hundred men; combat troops of one thousand nine hundred were taken as seventy-six squads; within the combat troops of each army there were three hundred crossbowmen, three hundred archers, five hundred cavalry, four hundred assault troops, four hundred surprise troops, and nine hundred baggage per army—making two thousand eight hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengyi and his colleagues began with Li Jing's six-flower formation, using roughly twenty thousand troops as the standard and organizing seven armies. Each rear-guard army numbered two thousand eight hundred men, of whom one thousand nine hundred combat troops formed seventy-six squads. In each army's combat force there were three hundred crossbowmen, three hundred archers, five hundred cavalry, four hundred assault troops, four hundred surprise troops, and nine hundred baggage handlers—two thousand eight hundred men per army.

sentences.zh: 帝諭近臣曰：

translations.literal: The emperor instructed close ministers, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his close ministers:

sentences.zh: 黃帝始置八陣法，敗蚩尤於涿鹿。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor first established the eight-formation method and defeated Chiyou at Zhuolu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor first devised the eight formations and defeated Chiyou at Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮造八陣圖於魚復平沙之上，壘石為八行。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang built the eight-formation diagram on the level sands at Yufu, piling stones into eight ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang laid out the eight-formation diagram on the flat sands at Yufu, stacking stones in eight ranks.

sentences.zh: 晉桓溫見之，曰：“常山蛇勢。

translations.literal: Jin-era Huan Wen saw it and said: "The Mount Chang snake posture.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen of Jin saw it, he said, "This is the coiling-snake formation of Mount Chang.

sentences.zh: ”此即九軍陣法也。

translations.literal: " This is the nine-armies formation method.
translations.idiomatic: " That is the nine-armies formation doctrine.

sentences.zh: 至隋韓擒虎深明其法，以授其甥李靖。

translations.literal: By Sui, Han Qihu deeply understood its method and transmitted it to his nephew Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui times Han Qihu mastered the method and passed it to his nephew Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 靖以時遇久亂，將臣通曉者頗多，故造六花陣以變九軍之法，使世人不能曉之。

translations.literal: Jing, because the age had long been in disorder and many generals and ministers understood it, therefore devised the six-flower formation to transform the nine-armies method, so that men of the world could not comprehend it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm had been torn by long disorder and many commanders already understood the old method, Li Jing devised the six-flower formation as a variant of the nine-armies doctrine so that others could not easily grasp it.

sentences.zh: 大抵八陣即九軍，九軍者，方陣也。

translations.literal: In general the eight formations are the nine armies; the nine armies are the square formation.
translations.idiomatic: In essence the eight formations are the nine armies, and the nine armies constitute the square formation.

sentences.zh: 六花陣即七軍，七軍者，圓陣也。

translations.literal: The six-flower formation is the seven armies; the seven armies are the round formation.
translations.idiomatic: The six-flower formation corresponds to seven armies, and the seven armies constitute the round formation.

sentences.zh: 蓋陣以圓為體，方陣者內圓而外方，圓陣即內外俱圓矣。

translations.literal: For formations take the round as substance; the square formation is round within and square without; the round formation is round within and without alike.
translations.idiomatic: Formations take the circle as their underlying form: a square formation is round within and square without; a round formation is round both inside and out.

sentences.zh: 故以方圓物驗之，則方以八包一，圓以六包一，此九軍六花陣之大體也。

translations.literal: Thus testing with square and round objects, the square uses eight to enclose one, the round uses six to enclose one—this is the general principle of the nine-armies and six-flower formations.
translations.idiomatic: Test this with square and round objects: a square encloses one center with eight sides, a circle with six petals—such is the broad principle of the nine-armies and six-flower formations.

sentences.zh: 六軍者，左右虞候軍各一，為二虞候軍；

translations.literal: The six armies: left and right rear-guard armies one each, making two rear-guard armies;
translations.idiomatic: The six armies are the left and right rear-guard armies—two rear-guard armies in all;

sentences.zh: 左右廂各二，為四廂軍；

translations.literal: left and right wings two each, making four wing armies;
translations.idiomatic: two wings on the left and two on the right—four wing armies;

sentences.zh: 與中軍共為七軍。

translations.literal: together with the center army making seven armies.
translations.idiomatic: together with the center army, seven armies in all.

sentences.zh: 八陣者，加前後二軍，共為九軍。

translations.literal: The eight formations add front and rear armies, together making nine armies.
translations.idiomatic: The eight formations add front and rear armies for nine armies in total.

sentences.zh: 開國以來，置殿前、馬步軍三帥，即中軍、前後軍帥之別名；

translations.literal: Since the founding of the dynasty, the three commanders of the Palace Guard Bureau and the mounted and foot armies were simply alternate names for the center, front, and rear army commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's founding, the three commanders of the Palace Guard and the mounted and foot armies have been alternate names for the center, front, and rear army commanders;

sentences.zh: 而馬步軍都虞候是為二虞候軍，天武、捧日、龍神衛四廂是為四廂軍也。

translations.literal: while the mounted and foot armies' rear-guard commanders were the two rear-guard armies, and the four wings of the Celestial Martial, Sun-Upholding, and Dragon Spirit Guards were the four wing armies.
translations.idiomatic: the mounted and foot armies' rear-guard commanders are the two rear-guard armies, and the four wings of the Celestial Martial, Sun-Upholding, and Dragon Spirit Guards are the four wing armies.

sentences.zh: 中軍帥總製九軍，即殿前都虞候，專總中軍一軍之事務，是其名實與古九軍及六花陣相符而不少差也。

translations.literal: The center army commander commanded all nine armies—that is, the Palace Guard rear-guard commander, who exclusively commanded the affairs of the one center army; thus name and reality accord with the ancient nine armies and six-flower formation without the slightest discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: The center army commander who commands all nine armies—that is, the Palace Guard rear-guard commander, who oversees the center army—matches the ancient nine-armies and six-flower systems in name and substance without the slightest deviation.

sentences.zh: 今論兵者俱以唐李筌《太白陰經》中陣圖為法，失之遠矣。

translations.literal: Those who discuss warfare today all take the formation diagrams in Tang Li Quan's Secret Classic of the Great White as their method—far astray indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Military theorists today all treat the formation diagrams in Li Quan's Tang Secret Classic of the Great White as authoritative— a grievous error.

sentences.zh: 朕嚐覽近日臣僚所獻陣圖，皆妄相眩惑，無一可取。

translations.literal: We have examined the formation diagrams recently submitted by officials—all falsely dazzle and deceive, not one usable.
translations.idiomatic: We have reviewed the formation diagrams recently submitted by officials; all are empty show, and not one is usable.

sentences.zh: 果如其說，則兩敵相遇，必須遣使豫約戰日，擇寬平之地，夷阜塞壑，誅草伐木，如射圃教場，方可盡其法爾。

translations.literal: If their doctrine were true, when two enemies met they would have to send envoys beforehand to fix a battle day, choose broad level ground, level mounds and fill ravines, cut grass and fell trees, like an archery ground or drill field—only then could the method be fully applied.
translations.idiomatic: If their doctrine were true, two armies could fight only after envoys had fixed a date in advance, chosen open ground, leveled hills and filled ravines, and cleared brush and trees like a parade ground—only then could the method be fully deployed.

sentences.zh: 以理推之，其不可用決矣。

translations.literal: Reasoning from principle, their unusability is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Reason alone shows they are unusable.

sentences.zh: 今可約李靖法為九軍營陣之製。

translations.literal: Now Li Jing's method may be adapted as the system of nine-army camp formations.
translations.idiomatic: We shall now adapt Li Jing's method into the nine-army camp-formation system.

sentences.zh: 然李筌圖乃營法，非陣法也。

translations.literal: Yet Li Quan's diagrams are camp methods, not formation methods.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan's diagrams describe camp organization, not battle formations.

sentences.zh: 朕采古之法，酌今之宜，曰營曰陣，本出於一法，特止曰營，行曰陣；

translations.literal: We take ancient methods and weigh present suitability: what is called camp and what is called formation originally spring from one method—only halted it is called camp, moving it is called formation;
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on ancient methods and adapting them to present needs, camp and formation are one doctrine: halted, it is a camp; in motion, a formation;

sentences.zh: 在奇正言之，則營為正、陣為奇也。

translations.literal: speaking in terms of regular and irregular forces, the camp is regular and the formation is irregular.
translations.idiomatic: in the language of regular and irregular deployment, the camp is the regular force and the formation the irregular.

sentences.zh: 於是以八月大閱八軍陣於城南荊家陂。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the eighth month a grand review of the eight-army formation was held at Jingjiapo south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: That August a grand review of the eight-army formation was held at Jingjiapo south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 已事，賜遂而下至指使、馬步軍銀絹有差。

translations.literal: When finished, Yang Sui and those below down to adjutants and mounted and foot troops were granted silver and silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: When the review ended, Yang Sui and his subordinates down to adjutants and mounted and foot troops received grants of silver and silk in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔諸路權住教五軍陣，止教四禦陣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict ordered all circuits temporarily to halt instruction in the five-army formation and to teach only the four defensive formations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict directed all circuits to suspend drill in the five-army formation and teach only the four defensive formations.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，帝於輔臣論營陣法，謂：“為將者少知將兵之理，且八軍、六軍皆大將居中，大將譬則心也，諸軍，四體也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, fourth month, the emperor discussed camp and formation methods with assisting ministers, saying: "Generals rarely know the principle of commanding troops; moreover, in both the eight-army and six-army systems the great general stands at the center—the great general is like the heart, the armies are the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, fourth month, the emperor discussed camp and formation doctrine with his chief ministers, saying, "Too few generals understand how to command troops. In both the eight-army and six-army systems the commander stands at the center—the commander is the heart, the armies the four limbs.

sentences.zh: 運其心智，以身使臂，以臂使指，攻左則右救，攻右則左救，前後亦然，則軍何由敗也！

translations.literal: Wielding mind and intelligence, using the body to command the arms and the arms to command the fingers—attack the left and the right rescues, attack the right and the left rescues, likewise front and rear—how then could the army be defeated!
translations.idiomatic: Direct the mind, move the body to command the arms and the arms to command the fingers—strike the left and the right responds, strike the right and the left responds, and the same for front and rear. How then could the army be defeated!

sentences.zh: 元豐四年，以九軍法一軍營陣按閱於城南好草陂，已事，獎諭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanfeng, the nine-army method's single-army camp formation was reviewed by inspection at Haocao Po south of the city; when finished, rewards and commendations were issued.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 4 the single-army camp formation of the nine-army method was inspected at Haocao Po south of the capital; afterward commendations were issued.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔：“已降五陣法，令諸將教習，其舊教陣法並罷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict said: "The five-formation method has been promulgated; order generals to drill in it, and all former formation instruction is abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict declared: "The five-formation method has been issued; all generals are to drill in it, and previous formation instruction is abolished.

sentences.zh: ”蓋九軍營陣為方、圓、曲、直、銳，凡五變，是為五陣。

translations.literal: " For the nine-army camp formation has square, round, curved, straight, and sharp—five transformations in all—making the five formations.
translations.idiomatic: " The nine-army camp formation has five variants—square, round, curved, straight, and sharp—constituting the five formations.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，高翔言，乞以禦陣與新陣法相兼教閱，從之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, Gao Xiang memorialized, requesting that defensive formations and the new formation method be taught together in instruction-review drill; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanyou 1 Gao Xiang memorialized asking that defensive formations be drilled alongside the new formation method; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 蓋元豐七年，詔專用五陣法，而舊教禦陣遂廢；

translations.literal: For in the seventh year of Yuanfeng an edict had ordered exclusive use of the five-formation method, and instruction in the old defensive formations was then abolished;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfeng 7 an edict had mandated the five-formation method alone, and drill in the old defensive formations was dropped;

sentences.zh: 至是，復令互教。

translations.literal: at this point, joint instruction was again ordered.
translations.idiomatic: now both were to be taught again in combination.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，復罷教禦陣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, instruction in defensive formations was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 3 drill in defensive formations was abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 大觀二年，詔以五陣法頒行諸路。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daguan, an edict ordered the five-formation method promulgated to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In Daguan 2 an edict ordered the five-formation method issued to every circuit.

sentences.zh: 高宗建炎元年，始頒樞密院教閱法，專習製禦摧鋒破敵之藝、全副執帶出入、短樁神臂弓、長柄刀、馬射穿甲、木挺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan under Emperor Gaozong, the Bureau of Military Affairs instruction-review method was first promulgated, specializing in the arts of defensive preparation, breaking the enemy vanguard, and defeating the foe; full armor and gear for entry and exit; short-post Divine Arm bow; long-handled saber; mounted shooting through armor; and wooden staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozong's first year of Jianyan the Bureau of Military Affairs instruction-review regulations were first issued, focusing on defensive combat, shattering enemy vanguards, full armor drill, short-post Divine Arm bow practice, long-handled saber, mounted archery against armored targets, and wooden staff work.

sentences.zh: 每歲擬春秋教閱法，立新格。

translations.literal: Each year spring-and-autumn instruction-review regulations were drafted and new standards established.
translations.idiomatic: Each year new standards were set for spring and autumn instruction-review drills.

sentences.zh: 神臂弓日給箭二十，射親去垛百二十步。

translations.literal: For the Divine Arm bow twenty arrows were issued daily; shooting at the target from one hundred twenty paces from the buttress.
translations.idiomatic: With the Divine Arm bow, twenty arrows were issued per day; archers shot at targets one hundred twenty paces from the rampart.

sentences.zh: 刀長丈二尺以上，氈皮裹之，引鬥五十二次，不令刀頭至地。

translations.literal: Sabers of one zhang two chi or more, wrapped in felt and leather; fifty-two draw-and-thrust repetitions without letting the blade tip touch the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Sabers at least twelve chi long, wrapped in felt and leather, were drawn and thrust fifty-two times without letting the tip touch the ground.

sentences.zh: 每營選二十人閱習，經兩閱者五十人為一隊，教習分合，隨隊多少，分隸五軍。

translations.literal: Each battalion selected twenty men for review drill; those who passed two reviews formed squads of fifty, drilling in splitting and combining; according to squad numbers they were assigned among the five armies.
translations.idiomatic: Each battalion chose twenty men for review; those who passed two reviews were formed into fifty-man squads to drill in splitting and combining, then assigned among the five armies according to squad strength.

sentences.zh: 每軍各置旗號，前軍緋旗，飛鳥為號；

translations.literal: Each army had its own flags and signals: the front army scarlet flags, birds as signals;
translations.idiomatic: Each army had its flags and signals: the front army bore scarlet flags with birds as its sign;

sentences.zh: 後軍皂旗，龜為號；

translations.literal: the rear army black flags, the turtle as signal;
translations.idiomatic: the rear army black flags with the turtle as its sign;

sentences.zh: 左軍青旗，蛟為號；

translations.literal: the left army green flags, the flood dragon as signal;
translations.idiomatic: the left army green flags with the flood dragon as its sign;

sentences.zh: 右軍白旗，虎為號；

translations.literal: the right army white flags, the tiger as signal;
translations.idiomatic: the right army white flags with the tiger as its sign;

sentences.zh: 中軍黃旗，神人為號。

translations.literal: the center army yellow flags, the divine figure as signal.
translations.idiomatic: the center army yellow flags with the divine figure as its sign.

sentences.zh: 又別以五色物號製招旗、分旗。

translations.literal: Separate rally flags and split flags were also made in five colors with object signals.
translations.idiomatic: Rally flags and split flags were also made in five colors with corresponding emblems.

sentences.zh: 舉招旗，則五軍以旗相應，合而成陣；

translations.literal: When the rally flag was raised, the five armies responded with their flags and combined into formation;
translations.idiomatic: Raise the rally flag and the five armies answer with their flags and combine into formation;

sentences.zh: 舉分旗，則五軍以旗相應，分而成隊。

translations.literal: when the split flag was raised, the five armies responded with their flags and divided into squads.
translations.idiomatic: raise the split flag and they answer and divide into squads.

sentences.zh: 左右前卻，或分藏為伏，或分出為奇，皆舉旗為號。

translations.literal: Moving left, right, forward, or back—or splitting to hide as ambush, or splitting out as surprise force—all were signaled by raising flags.
translations.idiomatic: Movement left, right, forward, or back; splitting to lie in ambush or detaching as a surprise force—all were signaled by flags.

sentences.zh: 更鳴小金、應鼓，備瞻望不及者。

translations.literal: Small bells and response drums were additionally sounded for those who could not see in time.
translations.idiomatic: Small bells and response drums supplemented the signals for men who could not see in time.

sentences.zh: 豫約伏藏之所，緩鳴小金即止，急鳴應鼓即奇兵出陣趍戰，急鳴小金即伏兵出。

translations.literal: Ambush hiding places were fixed in advance; a slow small bell meant halt; a rapid response drum meant surprise troops leave formation and rush to battle; a rapid small bell meant ambush troops emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Ambush positions were agreed in advance: a slow small bell meant halt; a rapid response drum sent surprise troops from formation into battle; a rapid small bell brought ambush troops out.

sentences.zh: 其春秋大教推賞，依海行格法。

translations.literal: Spring-and-autumn grand drill promotions and rewards followed the universally applied regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions and rewards from the spring and autumn grand drills followed the standard regulations.

sentences.zh: 李綱言：“水戰之利，南方所宜。

translations.literal: Li Gang said: "The advantage of naval warfare is what the south should employ.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang said, "Naval warfare suits the south.

sentences.zh: 沿河、淮、海、江帥府、要郡，宜效古製造戰船，以運轉輕捷安穩為良。

translations.literal: Commandery seats and key prefectures along the Yellow River, Huai, sea, and Yangtze should follow ancient models in building warships, taking maneuverability, lightness, speed, and stability as excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Command centers and key prefectures along the Yellow River, Huai, coast, and Yangtze should build warships on ancient models, valuing maneuverability, speed, and stability.

sentences.zh: 又習火攻，以焚敵舟。

translations.literal: They should also drill in fire attack to burn enemy vessels.
translations.idiomatic: They should also train in fire attack to burn enemy ships.

sentences.zh: ”詔命楊觀復往江、浙措置，河、淮別委官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yang Guanfu to proceed to Jiang and Zhe to take charge, and separate officials were appointed for the Yellow and Huai [rivers].
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yang Guanfu to oversee arrangements in Jiangsu and Zhejiang, with separate officials appointed for the Yellow and Huai river regions.

sentences.zh: 三年，親閱水軍於鎮江登雲門外。

translations.literal: In the third year, he personally reviewed the naval forces outside Dengyun Gate in Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the emperor personally reviewed the naval forces outside Dengyun Gate in Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，詔內殿按閱神武中軍官兵推賞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, an edict ordered review and reward of officers and soldiers of the Shenwu Central Army in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 1134, an edict ordered a review in the inner hall of the Shenwu Central Army's officers and soldiers, with rewards granted according to merit.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，臣僚言：“州郡禁卒，遠方縱馳，多不訓練，春秋教閱，臨時備數，乞申嚴舊制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, officials said: Prefectural Imperial Guard soldiers, allowed to roam freely in distant regions, mostly receive no training; spring and autumn instruction-reviews are merely filled with numbers at the last moment. We request strict enforcement of the old system.
translations.idiomatic: In 1154, officials memorialized: Prefectural Imperial Guard troops in distant postings roam freely and receive little training. Spring and autumn drill reviews are padded with numbers at the last minute. We ask that the old regulations be strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，詔：“比聞諸路州廂、禁軍、土軍，有司擅私役，妨教閱。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, an edict said: We have lately heard that in the various circuits, prefectural garrison troops, Imperial Guard, and local troops are privately employed by officials without authorization, obstructing instruction-review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1161, an edict declared: We have learned that across the circuits, prefectural garrison troops, Imperial Guard units, and local militia are being diverted to private service by officials, interfering with drill and review.

sentences.zh: 帥府其嚴責守兵勤兵歸營，訓練精熟，以備點視。

translations.literal: Command headquarters shall strictly hold responsible [those who keep] garrison and active troops from returning to camp, training them to full skill in preparation for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Command headquarters must strictly require that garrison and active troops return to camp, train to full proficiency, and stand ready for inspection.

sentences.zh: 孝宗乾道二年，幸候潮門外，次幸白石閱兵，三衙率將佐道駕，射生官兵就禦輦下獻所獲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao under Emperor Xiaozong, he visited outside Houchao Gate, then visited Baishi to review troops; the Three Yamen led officers and aides to escort the imperial procession, and hunting archers presented their catch beneath the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In 1166, Emperor Xiaozong visited the area outside Houchao Gate and then Baishi to review troops. The Three Yamen led their officers in escorting the imperial procession, and hunting archers presented their quarry beneath the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 是日，有數將獨手運大刀，上曰：“刀重幾何？

translations.literal: That day, several generals wielded great sabers with one hand alone. The emperor said: How heavy are the sabers?
translations.idiomatic: That day, several generals wielded great sabers single-handedly. The emperor asked: How heavy are those sabers?

sentences.zh: ”李舜舉奏：“刀皆重數十斤。

translations.literal: Li Shunju reported: The sabers all weigh several tens of jin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunju replied: Each saber weighs several tens of jin.

sentences.zh: ”有旨：“卿等教閱精明。

translations.literal: An imperial directive said: Your instruction-review is meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: Your drill and review work has been excellent.

sentences.zh: ”又諭陳敏曰：“軍馬衣裝整肅如此。

translations.literal: He also instructed Chen Min: The troops' horses, clothing, and equipment are so orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Chen Min: The troops' horses, clothing, and equipment are impressively disciplined.

sentences.zh: ”特錫賚鞍馬、金帶，士卒推賞有差。

translations.literal: He specially bestowed saddled horses and gold belts; soldiers received differentiated rewards according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: He specially granted saddled horses and gold belts, and soldiers received graded rewards according to merit.

sentences.zh: 四年，幸茅灘教閱。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he visited Maotan for instruction-review.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the emperor visited Maotan for a drill review.

sentences.zh: 舉黃旗，連三鼓，變方陣；

translations.literal: Yellow flags were raised; three drumbeats in succession, and [troops] shifted to square formation;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow flags were raised; after three drumbeats the troops shifted into square formation;

sentences.zh: 五鼓，舉白旗，變圓陣；

translations.literal: five drumbeats, white flags raised, shift to circular formation;
translations.idiomatic: after five drumbeats white flags were raised and the troops shifted into circular formation;

sentences.zh: 次二鼓，舉赤旗，變銳陣；

translations.literal: next two drumbeats, red flags raised, shift to wedge formation;
translations.idiomatic: then after two more drumbeats red flags were raised and the troops shifted into wedge formation;

sentences.zh: 青旗，變直陣。

translations.literal: green flags, shift to linear formation.
translations.idiomatic: green flags were raised and the troops shifted into linear formation.

sentences.zh: 畢事，上大悅，賞賚加倍。

translations.literal: When finished, the emperor was greatly pleased and doubled the rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the review was complete, the emperor was greatly pleased and doubled the rewards.

sentences.zh: 兵分東西，呈大刀、火炮，上問李舜舉：“按閱比曩時如何？

translations.literal: Troops divided east and west, displaying great sabers and cannon. The emperor asked Li Shunju: How does this review compare with earlier ones?
translations.idiomatic: Troops divided into eastern and western formations, displaying great sabers and cannon. The emperor asked Li Shunju: How does this review compare with earlier ones?

sentences.zh: ”舜舉奏：“今日之兵，陛下親訓練，撫以深恩，錫以重賞，忠勇倍常。

translations.literal: Shunju reported: Today's soldiers, personally trained by Your Majesty, nurtured with deep grace and granted heavy rewards, are doubly loyal and brave.
translations.idiomatic: Shunju replied: Today's soldiers, trained personally by Your Majesty, nurtured with deep kindness and rewarded generously, are twice as loyal and brave as before.

sentences.zh: 乾道中，詔弓箭手元射一石四斗力升加三斗，元射一石力升加五斗，弩手元射四石力升加五斗，元射兩石七斗力升加八斗，進秩推賞有差。

translations.literal: During the Qiandao era, an edict [ordered]: archers originally shooting one picul four tenths strength promoted with three tenths added; originally shooting one picul promoted with five tenths added; crossbowmen originally shooting four piculs promoted with five tenths added; originally shooting two piculs seven tenths promoted with eight tenths added; rank advancement and rewards were differentiated.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiandao era, an edict ordered promotion standards for archers and crossbowmen who increased their draw weight: archers who had drawn one picul four tenths received a three-tenth increment for promotion; those who had drawn one picul received five tenths; crossbowmen who had drawn four piculs received five tenths; those who had drawn two piculs seven tenths received eight tenths. Rank advancement and rewards varied accordingly.

sentences.zh: 宰執進射親賞格，虞允文曰：“拍試以鬥力升請給，今用射親定賞，恐不加意鬥力。

translations.literal: The chief ministers presented reward standards for close-range shooting. Yu Yunwen said: Trial testing uses draw-strength increments to determine pay; now using close-range shooting to set rewards, I fear they will not concentrate on draw-strength.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers presented reward standards based on close-range shooting. Yu Yunwen objected: Trial examinations use draw-weight increments to determine pay. If rewards are now based on close-range shooting alone, soldiers may neglect building draw strength.

sentences.zh: ”上曰：“然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed: That is so.

sentences.zh: 他日雖強弓弩可以取勝，若止習射親，則鬥力不進。

translations.literal: In the future, though strong bows and crossbows can win victory, if they only practice close-range shooting, draw-strength will not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Strong bows and crossbows may win battles in the future, but if soldiers practice only close-range shooting, their draw strength will never improve.

sentences.zh: 此賞格不須行。

translations.literal: These reward standards need not be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: These reward standards should not be implemented.

sentences.zh: 淳熙間，立槍手及射鐵簾格。

translations.literal: During the Chunxi era, standards were established for spearmen and shooting at iron curtains.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunxi era, standards were established for spearmen and for shooting at iron curtain targets.

sentences.zh: 上謂輔臣曰：“聞射鐵簾，諸軍鼓躍奮厲。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his chief ministers: I hear that when shooting at iron curtains, all armies drum, leap, and strive vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers: I hear that when troops shoot at iron curtain targets, every army drums and leaps with fierce enthusiasm.

sentences.zh: ”周必大曰：“兵久不用，此輩無進取，自然氣惰。

translations.literal: Zhou Bida said: Troops long unused, these men have no ambition for advance, and naturally their spirit is slack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bida replied: With troops long unused in battle, these men lack ambition and naturally grow slack in spirit.

sentences.zh: 今陛下激勸告戒，人人皆勝兵。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty stimulates, encourages, and admonishes them; every man is a victorious soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's encouragement and admonition have made every man a match-ready soldier.

sentences.zh: ”於是殿前、步軍司諸軍及馬軍舊司弓弩手，射鐵簾合格兵共一千八百四十餘。

translations.literal: Thereupon among all armies of the Palace and Infantry Bureaus and crossbowmen of the old Cavalry Bureau, qualified soldiers in iron-curtain shooting totaled more than 1,840.
translations.idiomatic: Across all armies of the Palace and Infantry Bureaus and the Cavalry Bureau's crossbowmen, more than 1,840 soldiers qualified at iron-curtain shooting.

sentences.zh: 詔中垛簾弓箭手一石二斗力十箭，弩手四石力八箭，依格進兩秩，各賜錢百緡；

translations.literal: An edict [ordered]: archers hitting the curtain target with one picul two tenths strength and ten arrows, crossbowmen with four piculs strength and eight arrows, promoted two ranks according to the standard, each granted one hundred strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that archers who hit the curtain target with a one-picul-two-tenths bow using ten arrows, and crossbowmen who qualified with a four-picul weapon using eight arrows, be promoted two ranks and each granted one hundred strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 弓箭手一石力十箭以上，弩手三石力八箭，各進兩秩。

translations.literal: archers with one picul strength and ten arrows or more, crossbowmen with three piculs strength and eight arrows, each promoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: archers who qualified with a one-picul bow and ten or more arrows, and crossbowmen with a three-picul weapon and eight arrows, were each promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 詔中外諸軍賞格亦如之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered reward standards for all armies inside and outside [the capital] likewise.
translations.idiomatic: An edict extended these reward standards to all armies throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 二年，樞密院言：“殿、步司諸軍弓箭手，帶甲六十步射，一石二斗力，箭十二，六箭中垛為本等。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: Palace and Infantry Bureau archers, shooting in armor at sixty paces, one picul two tenths strength, twelve arrows, six arrows hitting the target mound as the base grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: For Palace and Infantry Bureau archers, the base standard is shooting in armor at sixty paces with a one-picul-two-tenths bow, twelve arrows, with six hits on the target mound.

sentences.zh: 弩手，帶甲百步射，四石力，箭十二，五箭中垛為本等。

translations.literal: Crossbowmen, shooting in armor at one hundred paces, four piculs strength, twelve arrows, five arrows hitting the target mound as the base grade.
translations.idiomatic: For crossbowmen, the base standard is shooting in armor at one hundred paces with a four-picul weapon, twelve arrows, with five hits on the target mound.

sentences.zh: 槍手，駐足舉手攛刺，以四十攛為本等。

translations.literal: Spearmen, standing firm and thrusting upward, forty thrusts as the base grade.
translations.idiomatic: For spearmen, the base standard is forty upward thrusts delivered from a firm stance.

sentences.zh: 主帥委統製、統領較其藝。

translations.literal: The commanding general entrusts regimental and battalion commanders to compare their skills.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding generals delegate regimental and battalion commanders to assess their men's skills.

sentences.zh: 本等外取升加多者，每軍五千五百人以上弓、弩、槍手各十五人，詣主帥審實，上樞密院覆試。

translations.literal: Beyond the base grade, those with the most added increments—in each army of 5,500 or more, fifteen archers, crossbowmen, and spearmen each—proceed to the commanding general for verification, then to the Bureau of Military Affairs for re-testing.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the base grade, the fifteen archers, crossbowmen, and spearmen in each army of 5,500 or more who show the greatest improvement proceed to the commanding general for verification, then to the Bureau of Military Affairs for re-testing.

sentences.zh: 各擇優等二人升轉兩秩，餘人給錢五緡，俟將來再試。

translations.literal: From each group the two top performers are promoted two ranks; the rest receive five strings of cash, awaiting future re-testing.
translations.idiomatic: The two top performers in each group are promoted two ranks; the remainder receive five strings of cash and await future re-testing.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年，幸候潮門外大閱。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingyuan, he visited outside Houchao Gate for a great review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1196, the emperor held a grand review outside Houchao Gate.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，詔將按閱諸軍，賞賚依慶元二年增給。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiatai, an edict [said] when about to review all armies, rewards shall follow the increased grants of the second year of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1202, an edict ordered that when reviewing all armies, rewards be increased according to the Qingyuan second-year standard.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年，莫澤言：“州郡禁軍，平時則以防寇盜，有事則以備戎行，實錄於朝廷，非州郡可得私役。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoqing, Mo Ze said: Prefectural Imperial Guard, in peacetime to guard against bandits and robbers, in emergencies to prepare for military campaigns, are actually registered with the court and not available for private employment by prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In 1226, Mo Ze memorialized: Prefectural Imperial Guard troops serve in peacetime against bandits and in emergencies for military campaigns. They are registered with the court and must not be diverted to private service by prefectures.

sentences.zh: 比年州郡軍政隳廢，吝於廩給，闕額恒多。

translations.literal: In recent years prefectural military administration has decayed; they are stingy with rations, and vacancies are always numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years prefectural military administration has collapsed. Rations are withheld stingily and vacancies remain chronically unfilled.

sentences.zh: 郡官、主兵官有窠占，寓公有借事，存留者不什一。

translations.literal: Prefectural officials and officers in charge of troops have illicit holdings; retired officials borrow them for errands; those actually remaining are not one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural officials and military officers hold illicit allotments; retired officials borrow troops for personal errands. Fewer than one in ten soldiers actually remain in camp.

sentences.zh: 當教閱時，鈐、總、路分雖號主兵，僅守虛籍，莫敢號召。

translations.literal: At instruction-review time, supervisory, overall, and circuit officers though titled in charge of troops only maintain empty registers and dare not summon them.
translations.idiomatic: At drill review time, supervisory and circuit officers nominally in command maintain only empty registers and dare not summon the troops.

sentences.zh: 入教之次，坐作進退殆同兒戲。

translations.literal: When entering instruction, sitting, rising, advancing, and retreating are nearly like child's play.
translations.idiomatic: When troops enter drill, their marching is scarcely better than child's play.

sentences.zh: 守臣利虛券不招填，主兵受厚賂改年甲。

translations.literal: Prefects profit from empty vouchers without recruiting replacements; officers in charge of troops accept heavy bribes to alter age records.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects profit by leaving vacancies unfilled; military officers accept heavy bribes to falsify age records.

sentences.zh: 且一兵請給，歲不下百緡，以小計之，一郡占三百人，是虛費三萬緡也。

translations.literal: Moreover, one soldier's pay and rations, no less than one hundred strings per year; calculated on a small scale, one prefecture holding three hundred men wastes thirty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Each soldier's pay and rations cost at least one hundred strings per year. A prefecture holding three hundred ghost soldiers on its rolls wastes thirty thousand strings annually.

sentences.zh: 私役禁軍，素有常憲。

translations.literal: Private employment of Imperial Guard has always had fixed statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Private employment of Imperial Guard troops has always been prohibited by statute.

sentences.zh: 守帥辟園池，建第宅，不給餐錢；

translations.literal: Prefects and commanders develop gardens and ponds, build mansions, and provide no meal money;
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and commanders develop gardens and build mansions without paying meal allowances;

sentences.zh: 寓公去城遼絕，類得借兵，擾害鄉閭。

translations.literal: retired officials far from the city generally borrow troops and harass the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: retired officials living far from the city routinely borrow troops and harass the countryside.

sentences.zh: 近而輔郡至有寓公占四五百兵者。

translations.literal: Near the capital, even auxiliary prefectures have retired officials holding four or five hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Even near the capital, retired officials in auxiliary prefectures hold four or five hundred soldiers apiece.

sentences.zh: 良由兵官之權輕，而私占之禁弛也。

translations.literal: Truly because military officers' authority is light and the prohibition on private holding is lax.
translations.idiomatic: This stems from the weak authority of military officers and the lax enforcement of prohibitions on private holding of troops.

sentences.zh: 乞嚴戒監司、守倅等，止許借廂軍，仍不得妨教閱，餘官雖廂軍亦勿借。

translations.literal: We request strict admonition to supervisory officials, prefects, and deputies: only garrison troops may be borrowed, and still not obstruct instruction-review; other officials, even for garrison troops, must not borrow.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that supervisory officials, prefects, and deputies be strictly warned: only garrison troops may be borrowed, and even then drill must not be obstructed. No other officials may borrow troops, garrison or otherwise.

sentences.zh: 淳祐十一年，台臣條陳軍匠不閑閱習之弊：“按舊制，禁兵毋私役。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chunyou, censorial officials itemized the abuse of military artisans not practicing in idle time: According to the old system, Imperial Guard must not be privately employed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1251, censorial officials detailed the abuse of military artisans who never drill in their spare time: Under the old system, Imperial Guard troops must not be privately employed.

sentences.zh: 比歲凡州軍屯營駐紥之處，多循舊習，每一州軍匠無慮數百，官無小大各占破，而雕鏤、組繡、攻金、設色之事靡所不有。

translations.literal: In recent years wherever prefectural armies are garrisoned, old habits persist; each prefectural army has no fewer than several hundred artisans; officials great and small each occupy them, and carving, embroidery, metalwork, and coloring tasks are without exception present.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years, wherever prefectural armies are garrisoned, old habits persist. Each prefecture keeps several hundred military artisans, claimed by officials of every rank for carving, embroidery, metalwork, coloring, and every other craft.

sentences.zh: 工藝雖精，擊刺不習，設有小警，何能授甲？

translations.literal: Though their crafts are fine, they do not practice thrusting and stabbing; if there is a small alarm, how can they take up armor?
translations.idiomatic: Their crafts may be fine, but they never drill in combat. At the first alarm, how can they take up arms?

sentences.zh: 乞申嚴帥守及統兵官，應軍匠聽歸營伍閑習訓練，勿競作無益，虛糜廩稍，以妨軍實。

translations.literal: We request strict enforcement to commanders and officers in charge of troops: all military artisans should be allowed to return to their companies for idle-time practice and training; do not compete in useless work, wastefully consuming rations and obstructing military substance.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that commanders and military officers be strictly instructed to return all military artisans to their companies for drill in spare time, cease useless craft work, stop wasting rations, and restore military readiness.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳初，臣僚言：“諸軍統領、統製、正將、副將正欲在軍訓練，閑於武事，一有調用，令下即行，士悉將智，將悉士勇，所向無敵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianchun, officials said: Regimental commanders, battalion commanders, chief officers, and deputy officers are meant to train within the army and be skilled in military affairs; once an order comes, it is executed immediately; soldiers fully know their commanders' intent, commanders fully know their soldiers' courage; wherever they go, none can withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianchun era, officials memorialized: Regimental commanders, battalion commanders, chief officers, and deputies are meant to train within the ranks and master military affairs. When orders come, they march at once; soldiers know their commanders' minds and commanders know their soldiers' courage. Such armies are invincible.

sentences.zh: 今江南州郡、沿江製閫置帳前官，專任營運，不為軍計，實為家謀，絕無戰陣新功，率從帳前升差。

translations.literal: Now in Jiangnan prefectures and along the Yangzi, frontier commands appoint tent-ahead officers devoted solely to logistics, not planning for the army but actually scheming for their households; they have absolutely no new battlefield achievements, yet mostly rise through tent-ahead appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Today in Jiangnan prefectures and along the Yangzi, frontier commands appoint personal staff officers devoted solely to logistics — not for the army's benefit but for their own households. They win no battlefield honors yet rise through personal staff appointments.

sentences.zh: 大略一軍僅二三千，而使臣至五六百，以供雜役。

translations.literal: Roughly one army has only two or three thousand, yet envoys reach five or six hundred, to supply miscellaneous labor.
translations.idiomatic: An army of only two or three thousand men may have five or six hundred staff officers assigned to miscellaneous duties.

sentences.zh: 九年，臣僚言：“比者招募軍兵，一時徒取充數，以覬賞格。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, officials said: Recently when recruiting soldiers, they temporarily fill numbers to seek reward standards.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, officials reported: Recent recruitment fills ranks with anyone available simply to claim reward quotas.

sentences.zh: 涅刺之後，更不教閱。

translations.literal: After tattooing, they receive no further instruction-review.
translations.idiomatic: After tattooing, they receive no further drill or review.

sentences.zh: 主兵官苦以勞役，日夜罔休，一或少違，即罹囹圄，榜掠之酷，兵不堪命，而死者逃者接踵也。

translations.literal: Officers in charge of troops torment them with labor service day and night without rest; the slightest violation brings imprisonment; the cruelty of flogging is unbearable, and the dead and fugitives follow one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers torment them with corvée labor day and night without rest. The slightest infraction brings imprisonment. Flogging is so brutal that soldiers cannot endure it, and deaths and desertions follow one after another.

sentences.zh: 今請以新招軍分隸諸隊，使之熟紀律，習事藝，或旬或月上各郡閱試。

translations.literal: Now we request that newly recruited soldiers be distributed among the various squads, made thoroughly familiar with discipline, practice martial skills, and be reviewed monthly or every ten days in each prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that newly recruited soldiers be assigned to squads, drilled in discipline and martial skills, and reviewed monthly or every ten days in each prefecture.

sentences.zh: ”蓋弊至於此，而訓練之製大壞矣。

translations.literal: Abuses had reached this point, and the system of training was greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses had reached this point, and the training system lay in ruins.
